title.zh: 卷413 列傳二百 曾国荃弟：贞幹 沈葆桢 刘坤一
title.en: Volume 413 Biographies 200: Ceng Guoquan Younger Brother: Zhen Gan, Shen Baozhen, Liu Kunyi
title.raw: 卷413 列傳二百 曾国荃弟：贞幹 沈葆桢 刘坤一

sentences.zh: 列傳二百

translations.literal: Biographies 200
translations.idiomatic: Biographies 200

sentences.zh: 曾國荃弟貞幹沈葆楨劉坤一

translations.literal: Zeng Guoquan younger brother Zhen Gan, Shen Baozhen, Liu Kunyi
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Guoquan; his younger brother Zhen Gan; Shen Baozhen; Liu Kunyi

sentences.zh: 曾國荃，字沅甫，湖南湘鄉人，大學士國籓之弟也。

translations.literal: Zeng Guoquan, styled Yuanfu, a native of Xiangxiang in Hunan, was the younger brother of Grand Secretary Zeng Guofan.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Guoquan, whose style was Yuanfu, came from Xiangxiang in Hunan and was the younger brother of the grand secretary Zeng Guofan.

sentences.zh: 少負奇氣，從國籓受學京師。

translations.literal: In youth he possessed an uncommon spirit and studied under Guofan in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Even as a young man he showed unusual force of character and followed Guofan to study in Beijing.

sentences.zh: 咸豐二年，舉優貢。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xianfeng he was selected as an outstanding tribute student.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Xianfeng reign he passed the selection as an outstanding tribute student.

sentences.zh: 六年，粵匪石達開犯江西，國籓兵不利。

translations.literal: In the sixth year the Cantonese rebel Shi Dakai invaded Jiangxi and Guofan's army met with reverses.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year the Taiping commander Shi Dakai invaded Jiangxi, and Guofan's forces were hard pressed.

sentences.zh: 國荃欲赴兄急，與新授吉安知府黃冕議，請於湖南巡撫駱秉章，使募勇三千人，別以周鳳山一軍，合六千人，同援江西。

translations.literal: Guoquan wished to go to his brother's aid; he discussed the matter with the newly appointed prefect of Ji'an, Huang Mian, and requested of Hunan governor Luo Bingzhang permission to raise three thousand braves, with a separate force under Zhou Fengshan making six thousand in all, to reinforce Jiangxi together.
translations.idiomatic: Guoquan wanted to rush to his brother's relief. He and Huang Mian, the newly appointed prefect of Ji'an, petitioned Hunan governor Luo Bingzhang to let them raise three thousand militiamen; Zhou Fengshan's separate column would bring the total to six thousand, and the two forces would march together into Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 十一月，克安福，連破賊於大汾河、千金坡，進攻吉安，下旁數縣。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month he took Anfu, defeated the rebels in succession at Dafen River and Qianjin Slope, advanced against Ji'an, and reduced several neighboring counties.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month he captured Anfu, routed the rebels at Dafen River and Qianjin Slope in turn, pressed the attack on Ji'an, and brought several surrounding counties under control.

sentences.zh: 七年春，丁父憂回籍。

translations.literal: In the spring of the seventh year he returned home on mourning for his father.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the seventh year he went home to observe mourning for his father.

sentences.zh: 夏，賊麕聚吉安，周鳳山軍敗潰。

translations.literal: In summer the rebels gathered thickly at Ji'an and Zhou Fengshan's army was defeated and routed.
translations.idiomatic: That summer the rebels massed at Ji'an, and Zhou Fengshan's army was smashed and driven off the field.

sentences.zh: 時王珍、劉騰鴻皆喪亡，士氣衰沮。

translations.literal: At that time Wang Zhen and Liu Tenghong had both been killed, and army morale was shattered.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhen and Liu Tenghong had both fallen in battle by then, and morale had collapsed.

sentences.zh: 江西巡撫耆齡奏起國荃統吉安諸軍，軍復振。

translations.literal: Jiangxi governor Qiling memorialized to recall Guoquan to command all the Ji'an forces, and the army revived.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangxi governor Qiling memorialized to bring Guoquan back to take command of the Ji'an armies, and the troops recovered their fighting spirit.

sentences.zh: 冬，敗石達開於三曲灘，吉安圍始合。

translations.literal: In winter he defeated Shi Dakai at Sanqu Shoal and the siege of Ji'an was first closed.
translations.idiomatic: In winter he routed Shi Dakai at Sanqu Shoal, and the encirclement of Ji'an was finally drawn tight.

sentences.zh: 八年春，克吉水、萬安。

translations.literal: In the spring of the eighth year he took Jishui and Wan'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the eighth year he captured Jishui and Wan'an.

sentences.zh: 八月，督水師毀白鷺洲賊船，破城外堅壘，遂克吉安，擒賊首李雅鳳。

translations.literal: In the eighth month he directed the naval force to destroy rebel ships at Bailuzhou, broke the strong outer works, then took Ji'an and captured the rebel chieftain Li Yafeng.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month he ordered the river force to burn the rebel fleet at Bailuzhou, stormed the strong outer fortifications, and finally took Ji'an, capturing the rebel leader Li Yafeng.

sentences.zh: 以功累擢知府，撤軍還長沙。

translations.literal: For his merit he was repeatedly promoted to prefect and withdrew the army to Changsha.
translations.idiomatic: For these services he was promoted step by step to prefect and then led his troops back to Changsha.

sentences.zh: 九年，复赴江西，率硃品隆等軍五千餘人援剿景德鎮。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he again went to Jiangxi, leading Zhu Pinlong and others with a force of more than five thousand to assist in suppressing Jingdezhen.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he returned to Jiangxi at the head of more than five thousand men under Zhu Pinlong and others to help suppress Jingdezhen.

sentences.zh: 時諸軍與賊相持數月，莫肯先進。

translations.literal: At that time the various armies had faced the rebels for months without anyone willing to advance first.
translations.idiomatic: The allied columns had been locked with the rebels for months, and none of the commanders would move first.

sentences.zh: 國荃至，乃合力敗援賊於浮梁南。

translations.literal: When Guoquan arrived, they then combined strength and defeated the relief rebels south of Fuliang.
translations.idiomatic: Once Guoquan arrived, the columns finally joined forces and routed the relief army south of Fuliang.

sentences.zh: 三戰皆捷，火鎮市，追殲賊及半，克浮梁，擢道員。

translations.literal: Three battles were all victorious; they fired the market town, pursued and destroyed nearly half the rebels, took Fuliang, and he was promoted to circuit intendant.
translations.idiomatic: He won three engagements in a row, put the market town to the torch, hunted down and killed nearly half the enemy, and took Fuliang, for which he was promoted to circuit intendant.

sentences.zh: 江西肅清。

translations.literal: Jiangxi was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangxi was cleared of rebels.

sentences.zh: 國籓出九江，至黃州，與胡林翼議分路圖皖。

translations.literal: Guofan left Jiujiang and went to Huangzhou, where with Hu Linyi he discussed dividing forces to plan Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: Guofan marched out from Jiujiang to Huangzhou, where he and Hu Linyi worked out a plan to advance on Anhui along separate routes.

sentences.zh: 國荃留軍巴河，自還湖南增募為萬人。

translations.literal: Guoquan left the army at Bahe and himself returned to Hunan to raise recruits until he had ten thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Guoquan left his troops at Bahe and went back to Hunan to recruit until his command stood at ten thousand.

sentences.zh: 多隆阿、鮑超等既大破賊於太湖、潛山，十年閏三月，國荃乃進軍集賢關，規攻安慶。

translations.literal: After Duo Long'a, Bao Chao, and others had already inflicted a great defeat on the rebels at Taihu and Qianshan, in the intercalary third month of the tenth year Guoquan then advanced to Jixian Pass to plan the attack on Anqing.
translations.idiomatic: Once Duo Long'a, Bao Chao, and the others had shattered the rebels at Taihu and Qianshan, Guoquan in the intercalary third month of the tenth year moved up to Jixian Pass to lay siege to Anqing.

sentences.zh: 陳玉成來援，擊走之。

translations.literal: Chen Yucheng came to relieve the city; he was attacked and driven off.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yucheng marched to relieve the city, but Guoquan attacked and drove him away.

sentences.zh: 十一年，陳玉成復糾捻眾至於菱湖，兩岸築堅壘，與城賊更番來犯。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year Chen Yucheng again gathered Nian bands at Linghu, built strong forts on both banks, and with the city rebels took turns coming out to attack.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year Chen Yucheng rallied Nian auxiliaries at Linghu, threw up strong works on both shores, and with the garrison took turns sallying against the besiegers.

sentences.zh: 國荃調水師入湖，令弟貞幹築壘湖東以御之。

translations.literal: Guoquan moved the naval force into the lake and ordered his younger brother Zhen Gan to build forts on the east shore to hold them off.
translations.idiomatic: Guoquan sent the river flotilla into the lake and had his brother Zhen Gan throw up batteries on the eastern shore to block them.

sentences.zh: 會陳玉成在桐城為多隆阿所敗，還趨集賢關，迎擊破之。

translations.literal: As it happened Chen Yucheng had been defeated by Duo Long'a at Tongcheng; he hurried back toward Jixian Pass and was met and broken in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yucheng had just been beaten by Duo Long'a at Tongcheng; as he rushed back toward Jixian Pass, Guoquan met him and routed his column.

sentences.zh: 玉成由馬踏石遁走，仍留黨踞赤岡嶺，與菱湖賊壘犄角。

translations.literal: Yucheng escaped by way of Mata Stone, but still left a party holding Chigang Ridge, pincering with the Linghu rebel forts.
translations.idiomatic: Yucheng slipped away through Mata Stone, yet left a detachment on Chigang Ridge to work in tandem with the Linghu forts.

sentences.zh: 國荃困以長壕，鮑超來，合攻，悉破其壘，擒斬萬餘。

translations.literal: Guoquan penned them with a long trench; Bao Chao arrived and they attacked together, breaking all the forts and capturing or killing more than ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Guoquan hemmed them in with a long entrenchment; when Bao Chao came up they stormed the works together, smashed every fort, and killed or captured more than ten thousand men.

sentences.zh: 進破安慶城外賊營，毀東門月城。

translations.literal: He advanced and broke the rebel camps outside Anqing and destroyed the eastern gate barbican.
translations.idiomatic: He then overran the rebel camps outside the walls and tore down the barbican at the east gate.

sentences.zh: 惟北門三石壘堅不可下，令降將程學啟選死士緣砲穴入，拔之。

translations.literal: Only the three stone forts at the north gate were so strong they could not be taken; he ordered the surrendered general Cheng Qikai to choose dare-to-die men to enter along the gun embrasures and pull them out.
translations.idiomatic: Only three stone redoubts at the north gate still held out; he had the defector Cheng Qikai pick volunteers to crawl in through the embrasures and take them.

sentences.zh: 陳玉成屢為多隆阿所創，收餘眾，糾合捻匪，复屯集賢關，襲官軍後路，城賊葉芸來亦傾巢出撲。

translations.literal: Chen Yucheng had repeatedly been wounded by Duo Long'a; he gathered his remnants, mustered Nian bandits, again encamped at Jixian Pass, and struck at the government army's rear, while the city rebel Ye Yunlai also came out in full force to assault.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yucheng, battered again and again by Duo Long'a, rallied his survivors, called in Nian allies, and reoccupied Jixian Pass to threaten the imperial rear, while the garrison commander Ye Yunlai threw every man he had into the fight.

sentences.zh: 國荃憑壕而戰，屢擊卻，仍復進，增築新壘，遣貞幹合水師扼菱湖，絕賊糧路。

translations.literal: Guoquan fought from behind the trenches, repeatedly beating them back, then advanced again, built new forts, and sent Zhen Gan with the naval force to hold Linghu and cut the rebels' grain route.
translations.idiomatic: Guoquan held the entrenchments, drove assault after assault back, pushed forward again, threw up fresh works, and sent Zhen Gan with the flotilla to seal Linghu and starve the garrison.

sentences.zh: 八月，以地雷轟城，克之，殲賊萬餘，俘數千。

translations.literal: In the eighth month he blasted the wall with mines, took the city, destroyed more than ten thousand rebels, and captured several thousand.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month a mine blew in the wall; the city fell, more than ten thousand rebels were killed, and several thousand were taken prisoner.

sentences.zh: 捷聞，以按察使記名，加布政使銜，賜黃馬褂。

translations.literal: On report of victory he was placed on the list for provincial surveillance commissioner, given the rank of provincial administration commissioner, and granted a yellow riding jacket.
translations.idiomatic: When the victory was reported he was marked for promotion to provincial surveillance commissioner, given the rank of provincial administration commissioner, and awarded a yellow riding jacket.

sentences.zh: 尋以追殄餘賊，賜號偉勇巴圖魯。

translations.literal: Soon afterward, for pursuing and exterminating the remaining rebels, he was granted the title Weiyong Batulu.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, for hunting down the last bands of rebels, he received the honorific title Weiyong Batulu.

sentences.zh: 於是國籓進駐安慶，國荃率師東下規江寧，克無為州，破運漕鎮，拔東關，加頭品頂戴。

translations.literal: Thereupon Guofan advanced and encamped at Anqing; Guoquan led the army east to plan Jiangning, took Wuwei Prefecture, broke Yuncao Town, seized Dongguan, and was given the first-rank official's cap button.
translations.idiomatic: Guofan then moved his headquarters to Anqing while Guoquan marched east toward Nanjing, capturing Wuwei, storming Yuncao Town, and taking Dongguan, for which he received the first-rank cap button.

sentences.zh: 分兵守諸隘，自回湖南增募勇營。

translations.literal: He detached troops to hold the various passes and himself returned to Hunan to raise more brave battalions.
translations.idiomatic: He left detachments to hold the key passes and went back to Hunan to recruit additional battalions.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，授浙江按察使，遷江蘇布政使。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi he was appointed Zhejiang surveillance commissioner and transferred to Jiangsu administration commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tongzhi he was made surveillance commissioner of Zhejiang and then transferred to be administration commissioner of Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 詔以軍務緊要，毋庸與兄國籓迴避同省。

translations.literal: An edict stated that because military affairs were urgent, he need not observe the rule of avoiding the same province as his brother Guofan.
translations.idiomatic: The throne ruled that because the campaign was urgent, he did not have to observe the usual prohibition against serving in the same province as his brother Guofan.

sentences.zh: 三月，率新募六千人至軍，自循江北岸，令弟貞幹循南岸，彭玉麟等率水師同進，拔銅城徬、雍家鎮諸隘，复巢縣、含山、和州，克裕溪口、西梁山。

translations.literal: In the third month he led six thousand newly recruited men to the army; he himself followed the north bank of the river, ordered his younger brother Zhen Gan along the south bank, and Peng Yulin and others led the naval force forward together, taking the passes at Tongcheng Pang and Yongjia Town, recovering Chaoxian, Hanshan, and Hezhou, and capturing Yuxikou and Xiliang Hill.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month he brought six thousand fresh recruits to the front. He advanced along the north bank while Zhen Gan moved on the south; Peng Yulin's flotilla supported them. They seized Tongcheng Pang, Yongjia Town, and other strongpoints, recovered Chaoxian, Hanshan, and Hezhou, and took Yuxikou and Xiliang Hill.

sentences.zh: 渡江會攻金柱關，乘間襲太平，克之。

translations.literal: Crossing the river they joined to attack Jingzhu Pass, seized an opening to strike Taiping, and took it.
translations.idiomatic: They crossed the Yangzi to assault Jingzhu Pass together, then slipped in a strike at Taiping and captured it.

sentences.zh: 回克金柱關，貞幹亦剋蕪湖。

translations.literal: Returning they took Jingzhu Pass, and Zhen Gan also captured Wuhu.
translations.idiomatic: On the return march they secured Jingzhu Pass, and Zhen Gan took Wuhu as well.

sentences.zh: 令彭毓橘截敗賊於薛鎮渡口，大破之。

translations.literal: He ordered Peng Yuju to intercept and defeat the rebels at Xuezhen Ford and inflicted a great rout.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Peng Yuju to cut off the rebels at Xuezhen Ford and won a crushing victory.

sentences.zh: 五月，連奪秣陵關、大勝關要隘。

translations.literal: In the fifth month he seized in succession the strategic passes at Muling Pass and Dasheng Pass.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month he captured the vital passes at Muling and Dasheng in quick succession.

sentences.zh: 水師進扼江寧護城河口，陸師迳抵城南雨花台駐屯，賊來爭，皆擊卻之。

translations.literal: The naval force advanced to hold the Jiangning moat river mouth; the land force went straight to encamp at Yuhuatai south of the city, and whenever rebels came to contest the ground they were all beaten back.
translations.idiomatic: The river force moved up to block the mouth of Nanjing's moat while the infantry pitched camp on Yuhuatai south of the walls; every rebel attempt to drive them off was repulsed.

sentences.zh: 國籓猶以孤軍深入為慮，國荃謂：「舍老巢勿攻，浪戰無益，逼城足以致敵。

translations.literal: Guofan still worried about a lone army advancing deep; Guoquan said: "If we do not attack the old nest but fight at random, it is of no use; pressing the city is enough to bring the enemy out.
translations.idiomatic: Guofan still feared that the column was overextended, but Guoquan replied: "Skirmishing away from their lair does no good; only by pressing the city will we draw them out.

sentences.zh: 雖危，事有可為。」

translations.literal: Though dangerous, the affair can still be done."
translations.idiomatic: It is risky, but the situation can still be turned."

sentences.zh: 會秋疫大作，士卒病者半。

translations.literal: Just then autumn plague broke out fiercely and half the soldiers fell ill.
translations.idiomatic: At that point autumn sickness swept the camps and half the men were down.

sentences.zh: 賊酋李秀成自蘇州糾眾數十萬來援，結二百餘壘。

translations.literal: The rebel chieftain Li Xiucheng gathered several hundred thousand men from Suzhou to relieve the city and built more than two hundred forts.
translations.idiomatic: The Taiping commander Li Xiucheng rallied several hundred thousand men from Suzhou and threw up more than two hundred camps around the siege lines.

sentences.zh: 國荃於要隘增壘，輔以水師，先固糧道。

translations.literal: Guoquan added forts at critical points, supported by the naval force, and first secured the grain route.
translations.idiomatic: Guoquan strengthened the key positions, backed them with the river force, and secured his supply lines first.

sentences.zh: 賊環攻六晝夜，彭毓橘等乘其乏出擊，破賊營四。

translations.literal: The rebels besieged them in a ring for six days and nights; Peng Yuju and others struck when they were exhausted and broke four rebel camps.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels pressed the siege for six days and nights straight; Peng Yuju and others counterattacked when the enemy flagged and overran four camps.

sentences.zh: 賊悉向東路，填壕而進，前仆後繼。

translations.literal: The rebels all pressed the eastern route, filled the trenches, and advanced, those in front falling while those behind pressed on.
translations.idiomatic: They massed on the eastern sector, filled the trenches, and hurled wave after wave forward.

sentences.zh: 國荃督軍抵禦，砲傷頰，裹創力戰，賊始退。

translations.literal: Guoquan directed the army in defense; a cannon ball wounded his cheek, but he bound the wound and fought on fiercely until the rebels at last withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Guoquan directed the defense in person; a shell fragment struck his cheek, yet he bandaged the wound and kept fighting until the enemy finally fell back.

sentences.zh: 李世賢又自浙江率十萬眾至，與秀成合攻，屢掘地道來襲，毀營牆，百計攻襲，皆未得逞。

translations.literal: Li Shixian also came from Zhejiang leading a hundred thousand men to join Xiucheng in the attack; they repeatedly dug tunnels to assault, destroyed camp walls, and tried every stratagem, yet none succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shixian marched in from Zhejiang with another hundred thousand men to join Xiucheng; they tried mining, breached the parapets, and exhausted every tactic, yet could not break the ring.

sentences.zh: 蕪湖守將王可升率援師至，國荃簡精銳分出，焚賊數壘，餘棄壘走，進擊，大破之。

translations.literal: Wang Kesheng, defending general at Wuhu, led relief troops up; Guoquan picked elite troops to sortie, burned several rebel forts, the rest abandoned their works and fled, and on pursuit he inflicted a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Kesheng brought reinforcements up from Wuhu; Guoquan sent picked troops out, burned several enemy camps, and when the rest abandoned their works and ran, he pursued and shattered them.

sentences.zh: 先後殲賊數万，圍乃解。

translations.literal: In succession they destroyed tens of thousands of rebels and the siege was then lifted.
translations.idiomatic: In the end they killed tens of thousands of rebels, and the relief army melted away.

sentences.zh: 秀成、世賢引去。

translations.literal: Xiucheng and Shixian withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Xiucheng and Shixian drew off their forces.

sentences.zh: 是役以病餘之卒，苦戰四十餘日，卒保危局，詔嘉獎，頒珍賚。

translations.literal: In this campaign, with troops still recovering from illness, they fought bitterly for more than forty days and at last preserved the perilous situation; an edict praised them and bestowed precious gifts.
translations.idiomatic: With half his men still sick, Guoquan had held the line for more than forty days of brutal fighting and saved the siege; the court praised him and sent rich rewards.

sentences.zh: 議者欲令乘勝退保蕪湖，國荃以賊雖眾，烏合不足畏，不肯退。

translations.literal: Advisers wished him to take advantage of victory and fall back to defend Wuhu; Guoquan held that though the rebels were numerous, as a mob they were not to be feared, and he refused to withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: Some urged him to pull back to Wuhu while he still had the upper hand, but Guoquan insisted that the enemy horde was only a rabble and refused to retreat.

sentences.zh: 二年春，國籓親至視師，見圍屯堅定，始決止退軍之議。

translations.literal: In the spring of the second year Guofan came in person to inspect the army; seeing the siege camps firm, he at last decided to stop the talk of withdrawing troops.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the second year Guofan inspected the front himself, saw how solid the siege lines were, and finally put an end to talk of withdrawal.

sentences.zh: 詔擢浙江巡撫，仍統前敵之軍規取江寧。

translations.literal: An edict promoted him to Zhejiang governor while he still commanded the forward army to plan the taking of Jiangning.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to governor of Zhejiang but kept command of the field army aimed at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 四月，攻雨花台及聚寶門外石壘，克之。

translations.literal: In the fourth month he attacked Yuhuatai and the stone forts outside the Gate of Gathering Treasure and took them.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month he stormed Yuhuatai and the stone redoubts outside the Gate of Gathering Treasure and carried them.

sentences.zh: 九洑洲為江寧犄角，賊聚守最堅。

translations.literal: Jiufu Island was the horn of Jiangning's defense and the rebels gathered there in the strongest hold.
translations.idiomatic: Jiufu Island was Nanjing's strategic anchor on the river, and the rebels held it with their stiffest garrison.

sentences.zh: 國荃偕彭玉麟、楊岳斌往覘形勢，合水陸軍血戰，克之，江面遂清。

translations.literal: Guoquan went with Peng Yulin and Yang Yuebin to reconnoiter the terrain; land and naval forces fought a bloody battle together, took it, and the river surface was then cleared.
translations.idiomatic: Guoquan went with Peng Yulin and Yang Yuebin to scout the ground; the combined river and land forces stormed it in a bloody fight, and once it fell the Yangzi was clear.

sentences.zh: 連克上方橋、江東橋，近城之中和橋、雙橋門、七甕橋，稍遠之方山、土山、上方門、高橋門、秣陵關、博望鎮諸賊壘，以次並下。

translations.literal: In succession he took Shangfang Bridge and Jiangdong Bridge, the nearer city works at Zhonghe Bridge, Shuangqiao Gate, and Qiweng Bridge, and farther out the rebel forts at Fang Hill, Tu Hill, Shangfang Gate, Gaoqiao Gate, Muling Pass, and Bowang Town, reducing them one after another.
translations.idiomatic: He then took Shangfang Bridge and Jiangdong Bridge, the inner ring at Zhonghe Bridge, Shuangqiao Gate, and Qiweng Bridge, and in turn the outer forts at Fang Hill, Tu Hill, Shangfang Gate, Gaoqiao Gate, Muling Pass, and Bowang Town.

sentences.zh: 國荃初至，合各路兵僅二萬，至是募圍師至五萬人。

translations.literal: When Guoquan first arrived, the combined forces of all routes were only twenty thousand; by now the recruited besieging troops had reached fifty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: When he first arrived he had barely twenty thousand men from all columns combined; by now his siege army had grown to fifty thousand.

sentences.zh: 十月，分軍扼孝陵衛。

translations.literal: In the tenth month he detached troops to hold Xiaolingwei.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he posted a detachment to block Xiaolingwei.

sentences.zh: 李鴻章克蘇州，李秀成率敗眾分佈丹陽、句容，自入江寧，勸洪秀全同走，不聽，遂留同城守。

translations.literal: Li Hongzhang took Suzhou; Li Xiucheng led his defeated troops scattered through Danyang and Jurong, himself entered Jiangning, urged Hong Xiuquan to flee together, was not heeded, and therefore remained to defend the city with him.
translations.idiomatic: After Li Hongzhang captured Suzhou, Li Xiucheng dispersed his beaten forces around Danyang and Jurong, slipped into Nanjing himself, and urged Hong Xiuquan to flee with him; when Hong refused, Xiucheng stayed to help hold the city.

sentences.zh: 三年春，克鍾山天保城，城圍始合。

translations.literal: In the spring of the third year he took Tianbao Castle on Zhong Hill and the encirclement of the city was first closed.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the third year he seized Tianbao Castle on Purple Mountain, and the ring around Nanjing was finally closed.

sentences.zh: 賊糧匱，城中種麥濟飢。

translations.literal: The rebels' grain was exhausted and within the city they planted wheat to relieve hunger.
translations.idiomatic: Supplies inside the city ran out, and the defenders sowed wheat in the streets to stave off famine.

sentences.zh: 國荃迭令掘地道數十處，賊築月圍以拒，士卒多傷亡。

translations.literal: Guoquan repeatedly ordered tunnels dug in dozens of places; the rebels built crescent entrenchments to resist and many soldiers were killed or wounded.
translations.idiomatic: Guoquan opened dozens of mining galleries in turn; the defenders threw up outer crescent walls to block them, and casualties mounted on both sides.

sentences.zh: 會詔李鴻章移師會攻，諸將以城計日可破，恥借力於人，攻益力。

translations.literal: Just then an edict ordered Li Hongzhang to move his army to join the assault; the generals reckoned the city could fall within days and were ashamed to borrow others' strength, so they pressed the attack all the harder.
translations.idiomatic: The court then ordered Li Hongzhang to bring his army to help, but the commanders believed the city would fall any day and were determined not to share the glory, so they redoubled their efforts.

sentences.zh: 鴻章亦不至。

translations.literal: Hongzhang also did not come.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hongzhang never showed up.

sentences.zh: 國荃慮師老生變，督李臣典等當賊砲密處開地道。

translations.literal: Guoquan feared the long siege would breed mutiny among the troops and directed Li Chengdian and others to open a tunnel where enemy fire was heaviest.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing that a prolonged stalemate would breed unrest in the ranks, Guoquan had Li Chengdian and others drive a gallery under the heaviest enemy batteries.

sentences.zh: 既成，懸重賞募死士，李臣典、硃洪章、伍維壽、武明良、譚國泰、劉連捷、沈鴻賓、張詩日、羅雨春誓先登者九人。

translations.literal: When it was finished he offered a heavy reward to recruit dare-to-die men; nine who vowed to be first over the wall were Li Chengdian, Zhu Hongzhang, Wu Weishou, Wu Mingliang, Tan Guotai, Liu Lianjie, Shen Hongbin, Zhang Shiri, and Luo Yuchun.
translations.idiomatic: When the mine was ready he posted a rich bounty for volunteers; nine officers swore to lead the assault: Li Chengdian, Zhu Hongzhang, Wu Weishou, Wu Mingliang, Tan Guotai, Liu Lianjie, Shen Hongbin, Zhang Shiri, and Luo Yuchun.

sentences.zh: 六月十六日，日加午，地道火發，城崩二十餘丈，李臣典、硃洪章等蟻附爭登。

translations.literal: On the sixteenth day of the sixth month, as the sun passed noon, the mine fired, the wall collapsed for more than twenty zhang, and Li Chengdian, Zhu Hongzhang, and the rest swarmed up like ants competing to climb.
translations.idiomatic: On the sixteenth of the sixth month, just past noon, the charge detonated and a twenty-zhang breach opened in the wall; Li Chengdian, Zhu Hongzhang, and the rest scrambled up the rubble in a frantic rush.

sentences.zh: 賊傾火藥轟燒，彭毓橘、蕭孚泗手刃退卒數人，遂擁入。

translations.literal: The rebels poured out gunpowder in a blast and fire; Peng Yuju and Xiao Fusi personally killed several retreating soldiers and then pressed in.
translations.idiomatic: The defenders ignited a powder cache in the breach; Peng Yuju and Xiao Fusi cut down several men who hung back, then drove the column through.

sentences.zh: 硃洪章、沈鴻賓、羅雨春攻中路，向偽天王府；

translations.literal: Zhu Hongzhang, Shen Hongbin, and Luo Yuchun attacked the center route toward the false Heavenly King's palace;
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Hongzhang, Shen Hongbin, and Luo Yuchun pushed up the center toward the Taiping palace;

sentences.zh: 劉連捷、張詩日、譚國泰攻右路，趨神策門，硃南桂等梯城入，合取儀鳳門；

translations.literal: Liu Lianjie, Zhang Shiri, and Tan Guotai attacked the right route toward the Divine Strategy Gate; Zhu Nangui and others entered by scaling ladders and together took the Yifeng Gate;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Lianjie, Zhang Shiri, and Tan Guotai took the right toward the Divine Strategy Gate while Zhu Nangui's men scaled the wall and together seized the Yifeng Gate;

sentences.zh: 其左路彭毓橘由內城至通濟門，蕭孚泗等奪朝陽、洪武門，羅逢元等從聚寶門入，李金洲從通濟門入，陳湜、易良虎從旱西、水西門入：於是江寧九門皆破。

translations.literal: On the left Peng Yuju went from the inner city to the Tongji Gate; Xiao Fusi and others seized the Chaoyang and Hongwu gates; Luo Fengyuan and others entered from the Gate of Gathering Treasure; Li Jinzhou entered from the Tongji Gate; Chen Chi and Yi Lianghu entered from the dry-land and water Ximen gates: thus all nine gates of Jiangning were broken.
translations.idiomatic: On the left Peng Yuju fought through the inner city to Tongji Gate; Xiao Fusi stormed Chaoyang and Hongwu; Luo Fengyuan entered by the Gate of Gathering Treasure; Li Jinzhou forced Tongji; Chen Chi and Yi Lianghu broke in from the western land and water gates—and with that all nine gates of Nanjing were in imperial hands.

sentences.zh: 守陴賊誅殺殆盡，猶保子城。

translations.literal: The rebels defending the battlements were nearly all killed, yet they still held the inner citadel.
translations.idiomatic: The defenders on the walls were cut down almost to a man, but a remnant still held the inner citadel.

sentences.zh: 夜半，自縱火焚偽王府，突圍走。

translations.literal: At midnight they themselves set fire and burned the false royal palace and broke out in flight.
translations.idiomatic: At midnight they torched the palace and tried to break out.

sentences.zh: 要截斬數百人，追及湖、熟，俘斬亦數百。

translations.literal: They were intercepted and several hundred were killed; pursued as far as Hu and Shu, several hundred more were captured or killed.
translations.idiomatic: Intercepting parties killed several hundred on the spot; pursuers caught up with them near Lake Tai and the town of Shu and killed or captured several hundred more.

sentences.zh: 洪秀全已前一月死，獲其屍於偽宮。

translations.literal: Hong Xiuquan had died the month before; his corpse was obtained in the false palace.
translations.idiomatic: Hong Xiuquan had died a month earlier; his body was found in the palace.

sentences.zh: 其子洪福瑱年十五六，訛言已自焚死，餘黨挾之走廣德。

translations.literal: His son Hong Fuzhen was fifteen or sixteen; a false report said he had burned himself to death, but the remaining party seized him and fled toward Guangde.
translations.idiomatic: His son Hong Fuzhen, fifteen or sixteen years old, was rumored to have died in the fire, but surviving rebels carried him off toward Guangde.

sentences.zh: 國荃令閉城救火，搜殺餘賊。

translations.literal: Guoquan ordered the city closed, fires extinguished, and the remaining rebels hunted down and killed.
translations.idiomatic: Guoquan sealed the city, put out the fires, and hunted down the last pockets of resistance.

sentences.zh: 獲秀全兄洪仁達及李秀成，伏誅。

translations.literal: Hong Xiuquan's elder brother Hong Renda and Li Xiucheng were captured and executed.
translations.idiomatic: They captured Hong Xiuquan's brother Hong Renda and Li Xiucheng and put them to death.

sentences.zh: 凡偽王主將大小酋目三千餘，皆死亂兵，斃賊十餘萬，拔難民數十萬。

translations.literal: In all more than three thousand false kings, chief generals, and chiefs great and small died in the turmoil; more than a hundred thousand rebels were killed and several hundred thousand refugees were rescued.
translations.idiomatic: More than three thousand Taiping princes, generals, and officers of every rank perished in the sack; well over a hundred thousand rebels were killed and several hundred thousand civilians were brought out to safety.

sentences.zh: 捷聞，詔嘉國荃堅忍成功，加太子少保，封一等伯爵，錫名威毅，賜雙眼花翎。

translations.literal: On report of victory an edict praised Guoquan for steadfast endurance and success, made him Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, enfeoffed him as a first-rank earl with the granted name Weiyi, and bestowed double-eyed peacock feathers.
translations.idiomatic: When the victory was reported, the court praised Guoquan's tenacity, appointed him Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, created him a first-class earl with the honorific name Weiyi, and awarded him the double-eyed peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 國荃功高多謗，初奏洪福瑱已斃，既而奔竄浙江、江西，仍為諸賊所擁，言者以為口實，遂引疾求退，遣撤部下諸軍，溫詔慰留；

translations.literal: Guoquan's merit was high and slander many; at first he reported Hong Fuzhen already killed, but afterward Fuzhen fled through Zhejiang and Jiangxi and was still upheld by the various rebels, and critics took this as a handle; he therefore pleaded illness to retire and sent orders to withdraw his subordinate armies, but a warm edict comforted him and urged him to stay;
translations.idiomatic: Guoquan's triumph drew envy as well as praise; he had first reported Hong Fuzhen dead, yet the boy soon turned up in Zhejiang and Jiangxi still at the head of rebel bands, giving his enemies fresh ammunition. Guoquan asked to step down on grounds of illness and began disbanding his troops, but the throne sent a gracious edict urging him to remain;

sentences.zh: 再疏，始允開缺回籍。

translations.literal: On a second memorial he was at last permitted to vacate his post and return home.
translations.idiomatic: Only after a second memorial was he allowed to resign and go home.

sentences.zh: 四年，起授山西巡撫，辭不就。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was recalled and appointed Shanxi governor but declined and did not take office.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was called back and offered the governorship of Shanxi, but he declined.

sentences.zh: 調湖北巡撫，命幫辦軍務，調舊部剿捻匪。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Hubei governor, ordered to assist in military affairs, and his old subordinates were transferred to suppress the Nian bandits.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Hubei as governor, told to assist in military affairs, and his former troops were ordered against the Nian rebels.

sentences.zh: 五年，抵任，汰湖北冗軍，增湘軍六千，以彭毓橘、郭松林分統之。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he reached his post, trimmed redundant Hubei troops, added six thousand Hunan Army men, and had Peng Yuju and Guo Songlin command them separately.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he took up the post, cut bloated Hubei units, added six thousand Hunan troops, and placed them under Peng Yuju and Guo Songlin.

sentences.zh: 時捻匪往來鄂、豫之交，國荃檄鮑超由棗陽趨淅川、內鄉防西路，郭松林由桐柏、唐縣出東路，劉維楨向新野為聲援。

translations.literal: At that time Nian bandits moved back and forth on the Hubei-Henan border; Guoquan dispatched Bao Chao from Zaoyang toward Xichuan and Neixiang to guard the western route, Guo Songlin from Tongbai and Tang County on the eastern route, and Liu Weizhen toward Xinye as a supporting demonstration.
translations.idiomatic: Nian bands were raiding along the Hubei-Henan border; Guoquan ordered Bao Chao from Zaoyang toward Xichuan and Neixiang to cover the west, Guo Songlin out from Tongbai and Tangxian on the east, and Liu Weizhen toward Xinye as a diversion.

sentences.zh: 賊折而北竄，詔郭松林越境會剿。

translations.literal: The rebels turned and fled north; an edict ordered Guo Songlin to cross the border and join the suppression.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels veered north, the court ordered Guo Songlin to cross into the neighboring province and join the pursuit.

sentences.zh: 是年冬，敗賊於信陽、孝感。

translations.literal: That winter he defeated the rebels at Xinyang and Xiaogan.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he routed them at Xinyang and Xiaogan.

sentences.zh: 賊竄雲夢、應城、德安，郭松林擊走之，克應城、雲夢，又敗之皁河、楊澤。

translations.literal: The rebels fled to Yunmeng, Yingcheng, and De'an; Guo Songlin attacked and drove them off, took Yingcheng and Yunmeng, and again defeated them at Zao River and Yangze.
translations.idiomatic: They fled into Yunmeng, Yingcheng, and De'an; Guo Songlin drove them out, recovered Yingcheng and Yunmeng, and beat them again at Zao River and Yangze.

sentences.zh: 松林追賊臼口，中伏受重傷，其弟芳珍戰死。

translations.literal: Songlin pursued the rebels to Jiukou, fell into an ambush and was severely wounded, and his younger brother Fangzhen died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Songlin pursued the enemy to Jiukou, walked into an ambush and was badly wounded, and his brother Fangzhen was killed in the fighting.

sentences.zh: 彭毓橘破賊於沙口，又敗之安陸。

translations.literal: Peng Yuju defeated the rebels at Shakou and again defeated them at Anlu.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Yuju routed the rebels at Shakou and beat them again at Anlu.

sentences.zh: 國荃以賊多騎，難與追逐，欲困之山地。

translations.literal: Guoquan held that the rebels had many horsemen and were hard to pursue, and wished to trap them in mountainous country.
translations.idiomatic: Guoquan judged that the Nian bands were too mobile to chase in the open and planned to pin them in the hills.

sentences.zh: 毓橘偕劉維楨屢戰不能大創，賊竄去。

translations.literal: Yuju together with Liu Weizhen fought repeatedly but could not inflict a great wound, and the rebels fled away.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Yuju and Liu Weizhen fought several engagements without a decisive blow, and the rebels slipped away.

sentences.zh: 總督官文與不協，國荃疏劾其貪庸驕蹇，詔解官文總督任。

translations.literal: He was at odds with Governor-General Guan Wen; Guoquan memorialized impeaching him for greed, mediocrity, arrogance, and insolence, and an edict removed Guan Wen from the governor-generalship.
translations.idiomatic: He clashed with Governor-General Guan Wen and memorialized against him as greedy, incompetent, and overbearing; the court dismissed Guan Wen from the post.

sentences.zh: 六年春，賊复犯德安，為劉銘傳、鮑超所敗，遁入河南境，尋復回竄。

translations.literal: In the spring of the sixth year the rebels again invaded De'an, were defeated by Liu Mingchuan and Bao Chao, fled into Henan territory, and soon returned to raid again.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the sixth year the rebels struck De'an again, were beaten by Liu Mingchuan and Bao Chao, fled into Henan, and soon doubled back to raid Hubei once more.

sentences.zh: 彭毓橘恃勇輕進，遇賊蘄州，戰歿於六神港。

translations.literal: Peng Yuju relied on his courage and advanced rashly, met the rebels at Qizhou, and died in battle at Liushen Harbor.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Yuju, overconfident in his bravery, pushed too far, met the enemy at Qizhou, and was killed at Liushen Harbor.

sentences.zh: 五月，捻匪長驅經河南擾及山東。

translations.literal: In the fifth month the Nian bandits drove straight through Henan and disturbed Shandong as well.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month the Nian columns swept through Henan and raided deep into Shandong.

sentences.zh: 詔斥諸疆吏防剿日久無功，國荃摘頂，下部議處，尋以病請開缺，允之。

translations.literal: An edict rebuked the frontier officials for long defense and suppression without success; Guoquan's cap button was removed, the case was sent to the ministries for deliberation, and soon he pleaded illness to vacate his post and was permitted.
translations.idiomatic: The throne rebuked the provincial commanders for months of failure; Guoquan was stripped of his rank insignia and referred for discipline, then resigned on grounds of illness and was allowed to go.

sentences.zh: 光緒元年，起授陝西巡撫，遷河東河道總督。

translations.literal: In the first year of Guangxu he was recalled and appointed Shaanxi governor, then transferred to director-general of the Hedong waterways.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Guangxu he was recalled as governor of Shaanxi and soon moved to head the Hedong waterways administration.

sentences.zh: 二年，復調山西巡撫。

translations.literal: In the second year he was again transferred to Shanxi governor.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was transferred back to Shanxi as governor.

sentences.zh: 比年大旱，災連數省。

translations.literal: In recent years great drought had struck and disaster linked several provinces.
translations.idiomatic: Years of severe drought had spread famine across several provinces.

sentences.zh: 國荃力行賑恤，官帑之外，告貸諸行省，勸捐協濟，分別災情輕重、賑期久暫，先後賑銀一千三百萬兩、米二百萬石，活饑民六百萬。

translations.literal: Guoquan vigorously carried out famine relief; beyond official funds he borrowed from various provinces, urged donations and mutual aid, distinguished severity of disaster and length of relief periods, and in succession disbursed thirteen million taels of silver and two million shi of grain, saving six million starving people.
translations.idiomatic: Guoquan threw himself into relief work: beyond the provincial treasury he borrowed from neighboring provinces, organized donations, and tailored aid to each district's needs. In all he distributed thirteen million taels and two million shi of grain and kept six million people alive.

sentences.zh: 善後蠲徭役，歲省民錢鉅萬。

translations.literal: In subsequent handling he remitted corvée labor and each year saved the people vast sums of money.
translations.idiomatic: In the recovery he waived labor levies, saving the people millions of cash each year.

sentences.zh: 同時荒政，山西為各省之冠，民德之，為立生祠。

translations.literal: Among famine administrations of the time Shanxi stood first among the provinces; the people were grateful to him and erected a living shrine.
translations.idiomatic: Among the famine relief efforts of the day Shanxi's was judged the finest; the people honored him with a living shrine.

sentences.zh: 六年，以疾乞罷，慰留，尋召來京。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he begged to retire on grounds of illness; he was comforted and retained, then soon summoned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he asked to retire because of illness; the court urged him to stay, then recalled him to Beijing.

sentences.zh: 七年，授陝甘總督，命赴山海關治防，复乞病歸。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was appointed Shaanxi-Gansu governor-general and ordered to Shanhaiguan to manage defense, but again pleaded illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was made governor-general of Shaanxi and Gansu and sent to fortify Shanhaiguan, but again pleaded illness and went home.

sentences.zh: 八年，署兩廣總督。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he served as acting governor-general of the Two Guangs.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he served as acting governor-general of Guangdong and Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 九年，內召。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was summoned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was called to the capital.

sentences.zh: 十年，署禮部尚書，調署兩江總督兼通商大臣，尋實授。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he served as acting minister of rites, was transferred to act as governor-general of the Two Jiangs and superintendent of trade, and soon received substantive appointment.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he acted as minister of rites, then as acting governor-general of Jiangsu and Jiangxi with charge of foreign trade, and soon received the posts in full.

sentences.zh: 時法蘭西兵犯沿海，中朝和戰兩議相持。

translations.literal: At that time French troops were violating the coast and at court the factions for peace and war were deadlocked.
translations.idiomatic: French forces were threatening the coast, and the court was split between advocates of peace and war.

sentences.zh: 國荃修江海防務，知上海關係諸國商務，法兵不能驟至，馭以鎮靜。

translations.literal: Guoquan repaired river and sea defenses, knew that Shanghai concerned the commerce of many nations and French troops could not arrive suddenly, and governed it with calm restraint.
translations.idiomatic: He strengthened coastal defenses, understood that Shanghai's trade tied in many foreign powers and that French troops could not strike the city overnight, and kept the port steady through the crisis.

sentences.zh: 詔遣文臣分赴海疆會辦，福建疆吏遂不能主兵。

translations.literal: An edict sent civil officials to the coast to handle affairs jointly, and the Fujian frontier officials then could not command the troops.
translations.idiomatic: The court dispatched civil commissioners to the coast, leaving Fujian's military commanders without authority over the troops.

sentences.zh: 國荃言權不可分，朝廷亦以其老於軍事，專倚之。

translations.literal: Guoquan said authority could not be divided, and the court also, because he was experienced in military affairs, relied on him exclusively.
translations.idiomatic: Guoquan insisted that command must not be split, and the court, trusting his long military experience, leaned on him alone.

sentences.zh: 命遣兵輪援台灣，原議五，實遣其三。

translations.literal: He was ordered to send gunboats to aid Taiwan; five had originally been agreed on, but only three were actually sent.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to send gunboats to Taiwan; five had been promised, but only three sailed.

sentences.zh: 坐下部議，革職留任。

translations.literal: The case was sent to the ministries for deliberation and he was dismissed from office but retained in his post.
translations.idiomatic: The ministries reviewed the case and stripped him of rank while leaving him in post.

sentences.zh: 兵輪終不得達，其二折至浙洋，助戰鎮海有功，和議尋定。

translations.literal: The gunboats in the end could not reach their destination; two of them turned to the Zhejiang coast, aided the fighting at Zhenhai with merit, and peace negotiations were soon settled.
translations.idiomatic: The ships never reached Taiwan; two diverted to Zhejiang and fought well at Zhenhai, and a peace settlement soon followed.

sentences.zh: 十一年，京察，以國荃夙著勳勤，開復處分。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, at the capital evaluation, because Guoquan had long shown merit and diligence, his penalties were restored.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year the capital evaluation restored his honors for his long record of service.

sentences.zh: 十五年，皇太后歸政，推恩加太子太保。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year the empress dowager returned power, and in extending grace he was made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year, when the empress dowager handed back the reins of government, he was promoted to Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent as part of the general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 國荃治兩江凡六年，總攬宏綱，不苛細故，軍民相安。

translations.literal: Guoquan governed the Two Jiangs for six years in all, grasped the broad outline, was not harsh over small matters, and army and people lived in mutual peace.
translations.idiomatic: For six years he governed the Two Jiangs, kept his eye on the large issues rather than petty disputes, and kept soldiers and civilians at ease.

sentences.zh: 十六年，卒於官，贈太傅，賜金治喪，命江寧將軍致祭，特諡忠襄，入祀昭忠祠、賢良祠，建專祠。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he died in office; he was posthumously made Grand Tutor, granted gold for the funeral, the Jiangning general was ordered to offer sacrifice, was specially given the posthumous title Zhongxiang, entered the Zhaozhong and Xianliang shrines, and a special shrine was built.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he died in office. The court posthumously made him Grand Tutor, funded his funeral, ordered the Jiangning general to conduct the rites, gave him the posthumous name Zhongxiang, enshrined him in the loyal-officials and worthy-ministers halls, and built him a private temple.

sentences.zh: 孫廣漢襲伯爵，官至左副都御史。

translations.literal: His grandson Guanghan inherited the earldom and rose to left vice censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Guanghan inherited the earldom and eventually became left vice censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 國荃弟貞幹，原名國葆。

translations.literal: Guoquan's younger brother Zhen Gan, originally named Guobao.
translations.idiomatic: Guoquan's younger brother Zhen Gan had originally been named Guobao.

sentences.zh: 諸生。

translations.literal: A licentiate.
translations.idiomatic: He held the licentiate degree.

sentences.zh: 從兄國籓剿平常德、寧鄉土匪。

translations.literal: He followed his elder brother Guofan in suppressing bandits in Changde and Ningxiang.
translations.idiomatic: He followed his elder brother Guofan in clearing bandits from Changde and Ningxiang.

sentences.zh: 時楊岳斌為把總，彭玉麟為諸生，貞幹亟稱於國籓，謂二人英毅非常，同闢領水師。

translations.literal: At that time Yang Yuebin was a platoon commander and Peng Yulin a licentiate; Zhen Gan repeatedly praised them to Guofan, saying the two were extraordinarily spirited and resolute, and together they opened the way to lead the naval force.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yuebin was then a platoon officer and Peng Yulin a degree holder; Zhen Gan kept urging Guofan to notice them, calling both men of rare drive, and together they helped launch the river force.

sentences.zh: 初敗於岳州，貞幹自引咎，言諸將無罪。

translations.literal: After the first defeat at Yuezhou, Zhen Gan took blame upon himself and said the generals were without guilt.
translations.idiomatic: After the first defeat at Yuezhou he blamed himself and insisted the other commanders were not at fault.

sentences.zh: 國籓東征，貞幹家居未從。

translations.literal: When Guofan marched east on campaign, Zhen Gan remained at home and did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: When Guofan marched east, Zhen Gan stayed home and did not join the campaign.

sentences.zh: 及其兄國華戰歿三河，貞幹誓殺賊復仇。

translations.literal: When his elder brother Guohua died in battle at Sanhe, Zhen Gan swore to kill the rebels and take revenge.
translations.idiomatic: After his brother Guohua fell at Sanhe, Zhen Gan swore to avenge him on the enemy.

sentences.zh: 胡林翼使領千人，自黃州轉戰潛山、太湖。

translations.literal: Hu Linyi had him lead a thousand men and from Huangzhou he fought through Qianshan and Taihu.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Linyi gave him a thousand men; he fought his way from Huangzhou through Qianshan and Taihu.

sentences.zh: 從國荃攻安慶，設計招降賊將程學啟，克城之功，學啟為多。

translations.literal: He followed Guoquan in attacking Anqing, devised a plan to induce the rebel general Cheng Qikai to surrender, and in the merit of taking the city Cheng Qikai contributed most.
translations.idiomatic: He joined Guoquan at Anqing, engineered the defection of the rebel commander Cheng Qikai, and Cheng did much of the work in taking the city.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，與國荃分路沿江進師，破魯港，克繁昌、南陵、蕪湖，會軍雨花台。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi he and Guoquan advanced along the river by separate routes, broke Lugang, took Fanchang, Nanling, and Wuhu, and joined forces at Yuhuatai.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tongzhi he and Guoquan advanced along opposite banks of the Yangzi, took Lugang, Fanchang, Nanling, and Wuhu, and rendezvoused at Yuhuatai.

sentences.zh: 尋染疫，將假歸，援賊至，被圍，強起任戰守，圍解而病劇，卒於軍。

translations.literal: Soon he contracted epidemic disease and was about to take leave to return home when relief rebels arrived and he was besieged; he forced himself up to command defense and attack, the siege was lifted but his illness grew severe, and he died in the army.
translations.idiomatic: He soon fell ill and was preparing to go home on leave when relief forces arrived and trapped the besiegers; he dragged himself from his sickbed to hold the line, the siege was broken, but his illness worsened and he died in camp.

sentences.zh: 初以功敘訓導，加國子監學正銜，賜號迅勇巴圖魯。

translations.literal: At first for merit he was ranked as director of studies, given the rank of director of studies in the Imperial Academy, and granted the title Xunyong Batulu.
translations.idiomatic: For his early services he was ranked as director of studies, given an Imperial Academy title, and awarded the name Xunyong Batulu.

sentences.zh: 既破援賊，擢知府，命下而貞幹已歿。

translations.literal: After the relief rebels were broken he was promoted to prefect, but the order came down after Zhen Gan had already died.
translations.idiomatic: After the relief army was routed he was promoted to prefect, but the appointment arrived after he was already dead.

sentences.zh: 事聞，贈按察使。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported he was posthumously made surveillance commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: On report of his death he was posthumously made surveillance commissioner.

sentences.zh: 李鴻章為陳戰績，詔依二品議卹，贈內閣學士，予騎都尉世職，建專祠，諡靖毅。

translations.literal: Li Hongzhang set forth his battle record; an edict ordered mourning benefits according to the second rank, posthumously made him a grand secretary, granted a hereditary commandant of cavalry post, built a special shrine, and gave the posthumous title Jingyi.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hongzhang summarized his campaigns; the court granted second-rank mourning honors, posthumously made him a grand secretary, gave his heirs a hereditary commandant's post, built a shrine, and named him Jingyi posthumously.

sentences.zh: 沈葆楨，字幼丹，福建侯官人。

translations.literal: Shen Baozhen, styled Youdan, a native of Houguan in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Baozhen, whose style was Youdan, came from Houguan in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 道光二十七年進士，選庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the twenty-seventh year of Daoguang, selected as a bachelor of the Hanlin Academy, appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the twenty-seventh year of Daoguang, entered the Hanlin Academy, and was appointed a compiler.

sentences.zh: 遷御史，數上疏論兵事，為文宗所知。

translations.literal: He was transferred to censor, repeatedly memorialized on military affairs, and came to the knowledge of Emperor Wenzong.
translations.idiomatic: He became a censor, memorialized repeatedly on military affairs, and won the notice of Emperor Wenzong.

sentences.zh: 咸豐五年，出為江西九江知府。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Xianfeng he went out as prefect of Jiujiang in Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Xianfeng he was appointed prefect of Jiujiang in Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 九江已陷賊，從曾國籓筦營務。

translations.literal: Jiujiang had already fallen to the rebels; he followed Zeng Guofan in managing camp affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Jiujiang had already fallen to the rebels, so he joined Zeng Guofan's staff to manage camp logistics.

sentences.zh: 六年，署廣信府。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he served as acting prefect of Guangxin.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he acted as prefect of Guangxin.

sentences.zh: 賊酋楊輔清連陷貴溪、弋陽，將逼廣信。

translations.literal: The rebel chieftain Yang Fuqing took Guixi and Yiyang in succession and was about to press Guangxin.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel leader Yang Fuqing captured Guixi and Yiyang in turn and was closing on Guangxin.

sentences.zh: 葆楨方赴河口籌餉，聞警馳回郡，官吏軍民多避走。

translations.literal: Baozhen was just going to Hekou to raise funds when he heard the alarm and galloped back to the prefecture; many officials, soldiers, and civilians fled.
translations.idiomatic: Baozhen was at Hekou raising funds when the alarm came; he raced back to find officials, troops, and civilians already fleeing.

sentences.zh: 妻林，先刺血書乞援於浙軍總兵饒廷選。

translations.literal: His wife, née Lin, first wrote a plea for aid in her own blood and sent it to Zhejiang army commander Rao Tingxuan.
translations.idiomatic: His wife, Lady Lin, pricked her finger and wrote a blood-letter begging Rao Tingxuan, the Zhejiang commander, for help.

sentences.zh: 會大雨，賊滯興安。

translations.literal: As it happened heavy rain fell and the rebels were delayed at Xing'an.
translations.idiomatic: Heavy rains then stalled the rebels at Xing'an.

sentences.zh: 廷選先入城，賊至，七戰皆捷，解圍去。

translations.literal: Tingxuan entered the city first; when the rebels arrived, seven battles were all victorious and the siege was lifted as they withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Rao entered the city first; when the rebels came he fought seven engagements and won them all, and the enemy withdrew.

sentences.zh: 曾國籓上其城守狀，詔嘉獎，以道員用。

translations.literal: Zeng Guofan reported his defense of the city; an edict praised and rewarded him and employed him as a circuit intendant.
translations.idiomatic: Guofan reported the defense of the city; the court praised him and appointed him a circuit intendant.

sentences.zh: 七年，擢廣饒九南道，留筦廣信防務。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was promoted to the Guangrao-Jiunan circuit and remained to manage Guangxin defense.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was promoted to the Guangrao-Jiunan circuit and stayed to oversee Guangxin's defenses.

sentences.zh: 數假客軍擊走竄賊，平弋陽土匪，誅安仁抗糧奸民，加按察使銜。

translations.literal: Several times he borrowed guest armies to drive off fleeing rebels, pacified bandits in Yiyang, executed treacherous subjects in Anren who resisted grain levies, and was given the rank of surveillance commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly borrowed allied troops to chase raiders, pacified bandits in Yiyang, executed grain-resisting ringleaders in Anren, and was given the rank of surveillance commissioner.

sentences.zh: 以伉直忤大吏，乞養親去官。

translations.literal: Because of his upright bluntness he offended a high official and begged to retire to support his parents, leaving office.
translations.idiomatic: His blunt integrity offended a senior official, and he resigned to care for his parents.

sentences.zh: 十年，起授吉贛南道。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was recalled and appointed to the Ji-Gan-Nan circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he was recalled and appointed to the Ji-Gan-Nan circuit.

sentences.zh: 以親老辭，未出，命留原籍治團練。

translations.literal: He declined because his parents were old and did not go out; he was ordered to remain in his native place to manage militia training.
translations.idiomatic: He pleaded that his parents were elderly and did not take up the post; he was ordered to stay home and organize local militia.

sentences.zh: 曾國籓屢薦其才，十一年，詔赴安慶大營委用。

translations.literal: Zeng Guofan repeatedly recommended his talent; in the eleventh year an edict ordered him to the great camp at Anqing for employment.
translations.idiomatic: Guofan recommended him repeatedly; in the eleventh year the court ordered him to the Anqing headquarters.

sentences.zh: 未幾，超擢江西巡撫，諭曰：「朕久聞沈葆楨德望冠時，才堪應變。

translations.literal: Before long he was promoted above the regular steps to Jiangxi governor; the instruction said: "We have long heard that Shen Baozhen's virtue and standing surpass his age and his talent can meet emergencies.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was promoted straight to governor of Jiangxi. The edict read: "We have long heard that Shen Baozhen's reputation stands above his contemporaries and that his talent meets every emergency.

sentences.zh: 以其家有老親，擇江西近省授以疆寄，便其迎養；

translations.literal: Because his family has aged parents, We choose a nearby province, Jiangxi, to entrust with frontier responsibility, to make it convenient for him to bring them for support;
translations.idiomatic: Because his parents are elderly, We assign him a neighboring province so he may bring them to live with him;

sentences.zh: 且為曾經仕宦之區，將來樹建殊勳，光榮門戶，足承親歡。

translations.literal: and moreover it is a region where he once served in office; in the future he may establish outstanding merit, bring glory to his household, and fully bear his parents' joy.
translations.idiomatic: and it is country he already knows, where he may yet win distinction, honor his house, and give his parents joy.

sentences.zh: 如此體恤，如此委任，諒不再以養親瀆請。」

translations.literal: With such consideration and such commission, We trust he will no longer plead to support his parents in irreverent refusal."
translations.idiomatic: With such consideration shown him, We trust he will not plead filial duty again to refuse."

sentences.zh: 葆楨奉詔，感泣赴官。

translations.literal: Baozhen received the edict, wept with gratitude, and went to take office.
translations.idiomatic: Baozhen received the edict, wept with gratitude, and took up the post.

sentences.zh: 時浙江淪陷，左宗棠由江西進軍規复。

translations.literal: At that time Zhejiang had fallen; Zuo Zongtang advanced from Jiangxi to plan recovery.
translations.idiomatic: Zhejiang had fallen by then; Zuo Zongtang was advancing from Jiangxi to recover it.

sentences.zh: 賊酋楊輔清、李世賢合擾江西，冀斷皖、浙運道。

translations.literal: The rebel chieftains Yang Fuqing and Li Shixian together harassed Jiangxi, hoping to cut the Anhui-Zhejiang transport route.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel leaders Yang Fuqing and Li Shixian raided Jiangxi together, hoping to sever the supply line between Anhui and Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，葆楨親赴廣信籌防，令士民築堡自衛，堅壁清野。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi Baozhen personally went to Guangxin to plan defense, ordered gentry and people to build forts for self-defense, and enforced clearing the countryside behind strong walls.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tongzhi he went to Guangxin in person to organize defense, had locals build stockades, and cleared the countryside behind walled strongpoints.

sentences.zh: 倚用湘將王德榜、段起及席寶田、江忠義諸人，客軍並聽指揮，賊至輒擊退。

translations.literal: He relied on Hunan generals Wang Debang, Duan Qi, and Xi Baotian, Jiang Zhongyi, and others; guest armies all obeyed his command, and whenever rebels came they were beaten back.
translations.idiomatic: He leaned on Hunan officers Wang Debang, Duan Qi, Xi Baotian, and Jiang Zhongyi; allied columns obeyed his orders, and every rebel probe was driven back.

sentences.zh: 二年，破黃文金於小路口，又破之於祁門。

translations.literal: In the second year he defeated Huang Wengin at Xiaolukou and again defeated him at Qimen.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he routed Huang Wengin at Xiaolukou and again at Qimen.

sentences.zh: 會浙軍克黟縣，賊由太平、石埭、建德擾江西，督軍進擊走之。

translations.literal: As the Zhejiang army took Yixian, rebels from Taiping, Shiji, and Jiande disturbed Jiangxi; he directed the army forward to attack and drive them off.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhejiang forces took Yixian, rebels slipped through Taiping, Shiji, and Jiande into Jiangxi; he led troops out and chased them off.

sentences.zh: 是年秋，因病請假。

translations.literal: That autumn he requested leave on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn he took sick leave.

sentences.zh: 初，曾國籓軍餉多倚江西。

translations.literal: At first Zeng Guofan's army funds relied heavily on Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: At first Guofan's army depended heavily on Jiangxi for funds.

sentences.zh: 葆楨以本省軍事方殷，奏留自給。

translations.literal: Baozhen, because military affairs in his own province were pressing, memorialized to retain funds for local use.
translations.idiomatic: Baozhen, with fighting still fierce in his province, memorialized to keep the revenue for local needs.

sentences.zh: 江寧前敵需餉亟，而江西協解不至，國籓疏爭。

translations.literal: The Jiangning front urgently needed funds, but Jiangxi's cooperative remittances did not arrive; Guofan memorialized in dispute.
translations.idiomatic: The Nanjing front needed money urgently, but Jiangxi's contributions did not arrive; Guofan protested in a memorial.

sentences.zh: 御史華祝三亦疏言兩人齟《齒吾》，慮誤大局，詔兩解之，命各分其半，別以江海關撥款濟江南軍。

translations.literal: Censor Hua Zhusan also memorialized that the two men were at odds and he feared harm to the overall situation; an edict had both reconcile, ordered each to share half, and separately allocated funds from the Jianghai customs to aid the Jiangnan army.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Hua Zhusan warned that their feud endangered the campaign; the court ordered them to settle, split the Jiangxi revenue equally, and allocated separate funds from the Shanghai customs for the Jiangnan army.

sentences.zh: 三年，大軍圍江寧急。

translations.literal: In the third year the great army's siege of Jiangning was urgent.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year the siege of Nanjing reached its crisis.

sentences.zh: 賊聚擾江西，圖牽後路。

translations.literal: Rebels gathered to harass Jiangxi, intending to pull at the rear route.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels massed in Jiangxi to threaten the besiegers' rear.

sentences.zh: 詔楊岳斌移師督剿，命葆楨會商機宜。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Yang Yuebin to move his army to supervise suppression; Baozhen was ordered to consult on the opportune course.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered Yang Yuebin to take command of the pursuit and told Baozhen to coordinate strategy with him.

sentences.zh: 既而江寧、杭州相繼复，黃文金擁洪福瑱由浙、皖竄江西，為入粵計。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Jiangning and Hangzhou were recovered in succession; Huang Wengin, upholding Hong Fuzhen, fled from Zhejiang and Anhui into Jiangxi, planning to enter Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: Nanjing and Hangzhou then fell in turn; Huang Wengin escorted Hong Fuzhen from Zhejiang and Anhui into Jiangxi, aiming for Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 葆楨令席寶田追剿，至石城，大破之。

translations.literal: Baozhen ordered Xi Baotian to pursue and suppress them; at Shicheng he inflicted a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Baozhen sent Xi Baotian in pursuit; at Shicheng Xi shattered the column.

sentences.zh: 陣擒洪仁玕、洪仁政、黃文英等，搜獲洪福瑱於荒谷中，皆伏誅。

translations.literal: In battle Hong Rengan, Hong Renzheng, Huang Wenying, and others were captured; Hong Fuzhen was searched out in a wild valley and all were executed.
translations.idiomatic: Hong Rengan, Hong Renzheng, Huang Wenying, and others were taken in battle; Hong Fuzhen was found hiding in a remote valley, and all were executed.

sentences.zh: 以擒首逆功，予一等輕車都尉世職，加頭品頂戴。

translations.literal: For the merit of capturing the chief rebel he was given a hereditary first-rank commandant of light chariots post and the first-rank cap button.
translations.idiomatic: For capturing the rebel heir he received a hereditary first-rank commandant's post and the first-rank cap button.

sentences.zh: 葆楨推功諸將，疏辭，詔嘉其開誠佈公，將士用命，且江西吏治民風，日有起色，宜膺殊賞，不允所請。

translations.literal: Baozhen attributed merit to the generals and memorialized to decline; an edict praised his openness and fairness, the officers and soldiers obeying orders, and moreover that Jiangxi's official governance and popular customs daily improved, deserving special reward, and did not grant his request.
translations.idiomatic: Baozhen credited his generals and tried to decline the honors; the court praised his fairness, the discipline of his troops, and the improving order in Jiangxi, refused his declination, and insisted on rewarding him.

sentences.zh: 尋乞歸養，溫詔慰留。

translations.literal: Soon he begged to return home to support his parents; a warm edict comforted him and urged him to remain.
translations.idiomatic: He soon asked to go home to care for his parents; a gracious edict urged him to stay.

sentences.zh: 四年，以親病請假省視，因防務急，未行，丁母憂，命治喪百日，假滿仍回任。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, because his parent was ill he requested leave to visit; because defense was urgent he did not go; he entered mourning for his mother and was ordered to observe the hundred-day funeral, after which leave ended he was still to return to duty.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he asked leave to visit his ailing father but could not go because of the emergency; when his mother died he was told to mourn for a hundred days and then return to office.

sentences.zh: 堅請終制，乃允之。

translations.literal: He firmly requested to complete the full mourning period and was then permitted.
translations.idiomatic: He insisted on observing the full mourning term and was finally allowed to do so.

sentences.zh: 六年，命為總理船政大臣。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was appointed minister in charge of the naval administration.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was appointed superintendent of the Foochow Navy Yard.

sentences.zh: 初，左宗棠創議於福州馬尾山麓瀕江設船廠，未及興工，宗棠調陝甘，疏言非葆楨莫能任。

translations.literal: At first Zuo Zongtang had initiated the plan to set up a shipyard on the riverbank at the foot of Mawei Hill in Fuzhou; before construction began Zongtang was transferred to Shaanxi-Gansu and memorialized that none but Baozhen could undertake the task.
translations.idiomatic: Zuo Zongtang had first proposed a dockyard on the Min River at Mawei near Fuzhou; before work began he was transferred to the northwest and wrote that only Baozhen could run it.

sentences.zh: 葆楨釋服，始出任事。

translations.literal: Baozhen left mourning dress and only then began to take up the work.
translations.idiomatic: After Baozhen ended his mourning, he took up the post.

sentences.zh: 造船塢及機器諸廠，聘洋員日意格、德克碑為監督。

translations.literal: For the shipyard dry dock and the various machine factories he engaged the foreign officers Prosper Giquel and Paul d'Aiguebelle as supervisors.
translations.idiomatic: He built the dry dock and machine shops under foreign supervisors Prosper Giquel and Paul d'Aiguebelle.

sentences.zh: 月由海關撥經費五萬兩，期以五年告成。

translations.literal: Each month fifty thousand taels were allocated from the customs, with completion expected in five years.
translations.idiomatic: The customs paid fifty thousand taels a month, with a five-year completion target.

sentences.zh: 附設藝童學堂，預募水勇習練駕駛。

translations.literal: An attached school for artisan youths was set up and sailors were recruited in advance to practice navigation.
translations.idiomatic: He added a technical school for apprentices and began training sailors in seamanship.

sentences.zh: 事皆創立，船材來自外國，煤炭亦購諸南洋，採辦尤易侵漁。

translations.literal: Everything was newly established; ship timber came from foreign countries and coal was also purchased from the Southern Seas, and procurement was especially prone to graft.
translations.idiomatic: Everything had to be created from scratch; timber came from abroad and coal from Southeast Asia, and procurement was especially vulnerable to corruption.

sentences.zh: 葆楨堅明約束，一無瞻徇。

translations.literal: Baozhen enforced rules strictly and showed favor to none.
translations.idiomatic: Baozhen enforced strict rules and showed favor to no one.

sentences.zh: 布政使周開錫為提調，延平知府李慶霖佐局事，皆為總督所不喜，齮齕欲去之，葆楨疏爭得留，籓署吏玩抗，以軍法斬之，眾咸驚服。

translations.literal: The provincial treasurer Zhou Kaixi served as chief coordinator, and Yanping prefect Li Qinglin assisted bureau affairs; all were disliked by the governor-general, who harbored grievances and sought to remove them; Baozhen memorialized in dispute and secured their retention; clerks in the provincial yamen were lax and defiant, and he executed one by military law, whereupon all were greatly awed and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Kaixi, the provincial treasurer, was appointed chief coordinator, with Yanping Prefect Li Qinglin assisting the bureau. The governor-general disliked them both and kept looking for pretexts to remove them; Shen Baozhen memorialized strenuously on their behalf and kept them in post. When clerks at the provincial yamen grew slack and defiant, he had one executed under military law, and the staff were thoroughly cowed.

sentences.zh: 九年，丁父憂，仍請終制，暫解事，服闋始出。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he entered mourning for his father, still requested to observe the full mourning period, temporarily relinquished office, and only resumed duty after the mourning term ended.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he took leave for his father's death, insisted on completing the full mourning observance, stepped aside from his duties temporarily, and returned to office only after mourning ended.

sentences.zh: 當其居憂，內閣學士宋晉疏請暫停船工，詔下酌議。

translations.literal: While he was in mourning, Grand Secretariat academician Song Jin memorialized requesting a temporary halt to ship construction; an edict was issued for deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: During his mourning period, Grand Secretariat academician Song Jin submitted a memorial asking that shipbuilding be suspended temporarily, and the court ordered the matter discussed.

sentences.zh: 葆楨上疏，略謂：「自強之道，與好大喜功不同，不可以浮言搖動。

translations.literal: Baozhen submitted a memorial, stating in summary: "The way of self-strengthening differs from craving great achievements for show; it must not be shaken by loose talk.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Baozhen submitted a memorial arguing, in essence: "Self-strengthening is not the same as grandiosity and vainglory; loose talk must not be allowed to derail it.

sentences.zh: 且洋員合同不能廢，機廠經營不可棄。

translations.literal: Moreover, contracts with foreign technicians cannot be voided, and operation of the machine works cannot be abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Foreign specialists' contracts cannot simply be cancelled, nor can operation of the machine works be abandoned.

sentences.zh: 不特不能即時裁撤，五年期滿，亦不可停。」

translations.literal: Not only can they not be cut off at once; even when the five-year term expires, work must not cease."
translations.idiomatic: The yards cannot be shut down immediately; they must not be halted even when the five-year term expires.

sentences.zh: 推論利害切至，詔嘉納之。

translations.literal: His reasoning of advantages and disadvantages was penetrating; an edict praised and adopted it.
translations.idiomatic: His analysis of costs and benefits was trenchant, and the throne approved the memorial with praise.

sentences.zh: 十一年，再蒞事。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, he again took charge of affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he resumed his duties.

sentences.zh: 先後造成兵艦二十艘，分佈各海口。

translations.literal: Successively twenty military vessels were completed and distributed to the various sea mouths.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty warships were built in succession and stationed at major coastal ports.

sentences.zh: 尋以匠徒藝成，議酌改船式，督令自造，不用洋員監督。

translations.literal: Soon, as craftsmen and apprentices had mastered their skills, it was proposed to adjust ship designs appropriately, and he supervised orders for self-building without foreign technician supervision.
translations.idiomatic: Once the craftsmen had mastered their skills, he proposed revising the ship designs and directing purely domestic construction, without foreign supervisors.

sentences.zh: 疏陳善後事宜，並如議行。

translations.literal: He memorialized setting forth follow-up measures, and all were carried out as proposed.
translations.idiomatic: He laid out follow-up measures in a memorial, and the court implemented them as he recommended.

sentences.zh: 十三年，日本因商船避風泊台灣，又為生番所戕，藉詞調兵，覬覦番社地。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, Japan, because a merchant vessel took shelter from wind at Taiwan and its people were again killed by raw savages, used this as a pretext to move troops and coveted aboriginal village land.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year, after a Japanese merchant ship sheltered from a storm off Taiwan and crew were killed by indigenous tribesmen, Japan used the incident as a pretext to deploy troops and eyed aboriginal lands.

sentences.zh: 詔葆楨巡視，兼辦各國通商事務。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Baozhen to inspect on tour and concurrently handle commercial affairs with the various nations.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Baozhen was ordered to inspect Taiwan and oversee treaty-port trade with foreign powers.

sentences.zh: 日兵已登岸結營，葆楨據理詰之。

translations.literal: Japanese troops had already landed ashore and pitched camps; Baozhen interrogated them according to reason.
translations.idiomatic: Japanese troops had already landed and encamped; Shen Baozhen challenged them on legal and moral grounds.

sentences.zh: 曉諭番族遵約束，修城築壘為戰備。

translations.literal: He instructed and warned the aboriginal tribes to observe constraints, and repaired walls and built ramparts as war preparations.
translations.idiomatic: He instructed the indigenous peoples to keep the peace, and fortified towns and built bastions against attack.

sentences.zh: 提督唐定奎亦率淮軍至，日人如約撤兵。

translations.literal: Provincial military commissioner Tang Dingkui also led Huai Army troops there; the Japanese withdrew troops as agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial commander Tang Dingkui brought the Huai Army as well, and the Japanese withdrew as agreed.

sentences.zh: 乃議善後事宜，疏陳福建巡撫宜移駐台灣，吏治軍政方能整頓，詔如所請。

translations.literal: Thereupon follow-up affairs were discussed; he memorialized that the Fujian governor ought to be relocated to garrison Taiwan so that civil administration and military affairs could be properly rectified; an edict approved the request.
translations.idiomatic: He then proposed follow-up reforms, urging that the Fujian governor be stationed in Taiwan so civil and military administration could be brought to order; the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 甫內渡，獅頭社番戕官滋事，光緒元年，復往，督唐定奎等伐山開道，攻破內外獅頭等社，毀其巢，脅從者次第就撫。

translations.literal: He had just crossed inland when Lion Head village savages killed officials and stirred trouble; in the first year of Guangxu, he went again, supervised Tang Dingkui and others in cutting mountains and opening roads, stormed inner and outer Lion Head villages and others, destroyed their nests, and those coerced into following submitted in order.
translations.idiomatic: Hardly had he returned to the mainland when tribesmen of the Lion Head communities killed officials and rose in revolt. In the first year of Guangxu he went back, directing Tang Dingkui and others to cut roads through the mountains, stormed the inner and outer Lion Head settlements, destroyed their strongholds, and gradually brought intimidated followers back under control.

sentences.zh: 中路、北路亦分軍深入，諸番皆聽約束。

translations.literal: The central route and northern route also divided forces to penetrate deeply, and all tribes obeyed constraints.
translations.idiomatic: Forces on the central and northern fronts pushed deep as well, until all the tribes submitted to authority.

sentences.zh: 先於琅玡增設恆春縣，至是奏設台北府，淡水、新竹、宜蘭三縣隸之；

translations.literal: Previously Hengchun county had been added at Langya; at this point he memorialized to establish Taibei prefecture, with Danshui, Xinzhu, and Yilan three counties subordinate to it;
translations.idiomatic: Hengchun County had already been established in the Langqiao region; he now memorialized to create Taibei Prefecture, subordinating the counties of Danshui, Xinzhu, and Yilan;

sentences.zh: 噶瑪蘭通判移駐雞籠山；

translations.literal: the Gamalan subprefect was transferred to garrison at Jilong Mountain;
translations.idiomatic: the Gamalan subprefect was relocated to Jilong (Keelung);

sentences.zh: 台灣府同知移駐卑南；

translations.literal: the Taiwan prefecture subprefect was transferred to garrison at Beinan;
translations.idiomatic: the Taiwan-fu subprefect was moved to Beinan;

sentences.zh: 鹿港同知移駐水沙。

translations.literal: the Lugang subprefect was transferred to garrison at Shuishua.
translations.idiomatic: and the Lugang subprefect was transferred to Shuishua.

sentences.zh: 連疏陳營伍積弊，請歸巡撫節制。

translations.literal: In consecutive memorials he set forth accumulated abuses in the camps and requested that they return to governor control and regulation.
translations.idiomatic: In a series of memorials he exposed longstanding abuses in the garrisons and asked that troops be placed under the governor's command.

sentences.zh: 購機器，開台北煤窯，為明遺臣鄭成功請予諡建祠，以作台民忠義之氣，並報可。

translations.literal: He purchased machinery and opened Taibei coal mines, requested posthumous titles and temple construction for Ming loyal subject Zheng Chenggong to rouse the loyalty and righteousness of Taiwan's people, and all were approved.
translations.idiomatic: He procured machinery and opened coal mines at Taipei, and secured approval to confer a posthumous title on Zheng Chenggong and build him a temple, so as to inspire loyalty among the people of Taiwan.

sentences.zh: 遂撤軍內渡，事竣，擢兩江總督，兼通商大臣。
