translations.literal: Thereupon troops were withdrawn inland across the strait; when affairs were concluded, he was promoted to governor-general of Liangjiang and concurrently minister of commerce.
translations.idiomatic: He then withdrew his forces to the mainland; when the assignment was complete he was promoted to Liangjiang governor-general and concurrent trade minister.

sentences.zh: 江南自軍事定後，已逾十年。

translations.literal: Jiangnan, since military affairs were settled, had already passed ten years.
translations.idiomatic: More than ten years had passed since the fighting ended in the Jiangnan region.

sentences.zh: 疆吏習為寬大，葆楨精覈吏事，治尚嚴肅。

translations.literal: Frontier officials were habituated to leniency; Baozhen scrutinized official business minutely; his governance favored severity.
translations.idiomatic: Border governors had grown used to leniency, but Shen Baozhen audited administration closely and governed with marked strictness.

sentences.zh: 屬吏懍懍奉職，宿將驕蹇者繩以法，不稍假借。

translations.literal: Subordinate officials served their duties in fear; veteran generals who were arrogant and obstinate were bound by law with no indulgence.
translations.idiomatic: Subordinates served in wary obedience; veteran generals who were arrogant or insubordinate were held strictly to the law, without favor.

sentences.zh: 尤嚴治盜，蒞任三月，誅戮近百人，莠民屏跡。

translations.literal: He was especially severe in governing bandits; within three months of taking office, nearly a hundred were executed and put to death; wicked commoners vanished from sight.
translations.idiomatic: He cracked down especially hard on banditry: within three months of taking office he had executed nearly a hundred men, and rogues vanished from the streets.

sentences.zh: 皖南教案，華教士誣良民重罪，親訊，得其受枉狀，反坐教士，立誅之，然後奏聞，洋人亦屈伏。

translations.literal: In the South Anhui missionary case, a Chinese priest falsely accused upright common people of heavy crimes; he personally interrogated, obtained their wronged condition, reversed judgment onto the priest, immediately executed him, and only then memorialized; foreigners also submitted.
translations.idiomatic: In the South Anhui missionary incident, a Chinese priest had framed innocent villagers on grave charges. Shen Baozhen examined the case personally, found they had been wronged, reversed the charges onto the priest, and executed him on the spot before reporting to Beijing; even the foreign parties acquiesced.

sentences.zh: 淮南引地以次歸复，濬河、積穀、捕蝗、禁種罌粟諸政，並實力施行。

translations.literal: Huainan irrigated lands were restored in succession; dredging rivers, storing grain, catching locusts, prohibiting opium poppy cultivation and other policies were all implemented with solid effort.
translations.idiomatic: The Huainan salt transit zone was gradually restored, and policies such as dredging rivers, building granaries, catching locusts, and banning opium cultivation were all enforced vigorously.

sentences.zh: 數以病乞退，五年，入覲，皇太后溫諭勉以共濟時艱，毋萌退志，自此遂不言病。

translations.literal: Several times he pleaded illness to retire; in the fifth year he came to audience; the Empress Dowager warmly instructed him to share in relieving the time's hardships and not harbor thoughts of withdrawal; from then he no longer spoke of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly asked to retire on grounds of illness. On an audience visit in the fifth year the Empress Dowager gently urged him to share in meeting the nation's difficulties and not think of quitting; thereafter he stopped mentioning illness.

sentences.zh: 是年十一月，卒於位，贈太子太保，祀賢良祠，立功各省建專祠，諡文肅。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of that year, he died in office; posthumously gifted Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, enshrined in the Worthy Officials Temple, special temples built in provinces where he had accomplishments, posthumous title Wensu.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office that November, and was posthumously made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, enshrined in the Hall of Worthy Officials, with commemorative temples erected in the provinces where he had served; his posthumous name was Wensu.

sentences.zh: 子瑋慶，賜舉人，襲一等輕車都尉世職；

translations.literal: His son Weiqing was granted juren status and inherited the first-rank Captaincy of Light Chariots as a hereditary office;
translations.idiomatic: His son Weiqing was granted the rank of provincial graduate and inherited the hereditary title of first-class Captain of Light Chariots;

sentences.zh: 瑜慶，恩廕主事，官至貴州巡撫。

translations.literal: Yuqing, enfeoffed by grace as a secretary, rose to Guizhou governor.
translations.idiomatic: Yuqing received a grace appointment as a department secretary and eventually became governor of Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 劉坤一，字峴莊，湖南新寧人。

translations.literal: Liu Kunyi, style Xianzhuang, was a native of Xinning in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kunyi, courtesy name Xianzhuang, was from Xinning in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 廩生。

translations.literal: A licentiate of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He was a government student (licentiate).

sentences.zh: 咸豐五年，領團練從官軍克茶陵、郴州、桂陽、宜章，敘功以教諭即選。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Xianfeng, he led militia following government troops to capture Chaling, Chenzhou, Guiyang, and Yizhang; for merit he was recorded as ready for immediate selection as instructor.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Xianfeng he led local militia with government forces to take Chaling, Chenzhou, Guiyang, and Yizhang, and was rewarded with eligibility for immediate appointment as a district instructor.

sentences.zh: 六年，駱秉章遣劉長佑率師援江西，坤一為長佑族叔而年少，師事之，從軍中自領一營。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, Luo Bingzhang sent Liu Changyou to lead troops to aid Jiangxi; Kunyi was Changyou's clan uncle but younger, took him as teacher, and in the army commanded a camp of his own.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year Luo Bingzhang sent Liu Changyou to reinforce Jiangxi. Kunyi was Changyou's younger clansman and became his protégé, commanding his own battalion in the field.

sentences.zh: 長佑既克萍鄉，令進戰蘆溪、宣風鎮，連破賊，逼袁州，招降賊目李能通。

translations.literal: After Changyou had taken Pingxiang, he ordered advance battles at Luxi and Xuanfeng Town, repeatedly defeating rebels and pressing Yuanzhou, receiving the surrender of rebel chief Li Nengtong.
translations.idiomatic: After Liu Changyou took Pingxiang, he ordered Kunyi to attack Luxi and Xuanfeng, won repeated victories, closed on Yuanzhou, and won over the rebel leader Li Nengtong.

sentences.zh: 於是降者相繼，守城賊何益發夜啟西門，坤一先入，复袁州。

translations.literal: Thereupon surrenders followed in succession; defending rebel He Yifa opened the west gate by night; Kunyi entered first and recovered Yuanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Defectors came in one after another; the defender He Yifa opened the west gate by night, and Kunyi entered first to recover Yuanzhou.

sentences.zh: 累擢直隸州知州，賜花翎。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Zhili prefect magistrate and granted the peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted in stages to magistrate of a Zhili prefecture and awarded the peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 七年，克臨江，擢知府。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, Linjiang was taken and he was promoted to prefect.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he helped take Linjiang and was promoted to prefect.

sentences.zh: 八年，長佑以病歸，坤一代將其軍。

translations.literal: In the eighth year Changyou returned due to illness; Kunyi replaced him in command of the army.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year Liu Changyou went home ill, and Kunyi took over his command.

sentences.zh: 偕蕭啟江渡贛江規撫州，克崇仁。

translations.literal: Together with Xiao Qijiang he crossed the Gan River aiming at Fuzhou, and took Chongren.
translations.idiomatic: With Xiao Qijiang he crossed the Gan to threaten Fu Prefecture and captured Chongren.

sentences.zh: 啟江在上頓渡為賊所困，往援，大破賊，遂復撫州，連克建昌，擢道員。

translations.literal: Qijiang at Shangdundu was besieged by rebels; he went to rescue, greatly defeated rebels, then recovered Fuzhou, and in succession took Jianchang, and was promoted to circuit intendant.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Qijiang was trapped at Shangdundu, Kunyi relieved him, routed the rebels, recovered Fu Prefecture, and took Jianchang in succession, earning promotion to circuit intendant.

sentences.zh: 九年，石達開犯湖南，坤一回援，解永州、新寧之圍，加鹽運使銜。

translations.literal: In the ninth year Shi Dakai invaded Hunan; Kunyi returned to reinforce, relieved the sieges of Yongzhou and Xinning, and was given the salt transport commissioner rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year, when Shi Dakai invaded Hunan, Kunyi marched back, lifted the sieges of Yongzhou and Xinning, and received the salt commissioner rank.

sentences.zh: 賊竄廣西，從劉長佑追躡，复柳州。

translations.literal: Rebels fled into Guangxi; following Liu Changyou in pursuit, he recovered Liuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels fled into Guangxi; Kunyi followed Liu Changyou in pursuit and recaptured Liuzhou.

sentences.zh: 長佑擢撫廣西，令坤一駐柳州清餘匪，悉平之，加布政使銜。

translations.literal: Changyou was promoted to Guangxi governor; Kunyi was ordered to garrison at Liuzhou to clear remaining bandits, all were pacified, and he received provincial treasurer rank.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Changyou became Guangxi governor, he left Kunyi at Liuzhou to mop up remnant bandits; Kunyi pacified them all and was given the provincial treasurer rank.

sentences.zh: 進攻潯州，十一年七月，拔其城，以按察使記名。

translations.literal: Advancing to attack Xunzhou, in the seventh month of the eleventh year the city was taken; he was registered by name for surveillance commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He besieged Xunzhou and took the city in the seventh month of the eleventh year, and was placed on the list for provincial surveillance commissioner.

sentences.zh: 石達開回趨川、楚，坤一扼之融縣，掩擊敗之，賊潰走入黔，授廣東按察使。

translations.literal: Shi Dakai turned back toward Sichuan and Chu; Kunyi blocked him at Rong county, ambushed and defeated him, rebels routed and fled into Guizhou; he was appointed Guangdong surveillance commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Dakai turned toward Sichuan and the middle Yangtze, Kunyi blocked him at Rong County, ambushed and routed him, driving the rebels into Guizhou; Kunyi was then made Guangdong surveillance commissioner.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，遷廣西布政使。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi, he was transferred to Guangxi provincial treasurer.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tongzhi he became Guangxi provincial treasurer.

sentences.zh: 劉長佑赴兩廣總督任，命坤一接統其軍，赴潯州進剿。

translations.literal: Liu Changyou went to the Liangguang governor-general post; Kunyi was ordered to take over his army and proceed to Xunzhou to advance suppression.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Changyou left for the Liangguang governor-generalship, Kunyi was ordered to take over his forces and continue the campaign at Xunzhou.

sentences.zh: 貴縣匪首黃鼎鳳，在諸匪中最狡悍，屢議剿撫，不能下。

translations.literal: Guixian bandit chief Huang Dingfeng, among all bandits the most cunning and fierce, repeatedly discussed for suppression or pacification, could not be brought down.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Dingfeng of Guixian was the craftiest and toughest of the rebel chiefs; repeated campaigns of force and persuasion failed to subdue him.

sentences.zh: 二年，坤一破之於登龍橋，遂駐守之。

translations.literal: In the second year, Kunyi defeated him at Denglong Bridge and then garrisoned there.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year Kunyi defeated him at Denglong Bridge and encamped there.

sentences.zh: 鼎鳳老巢曰平天寨，倚山險樹重柵，守以巨砲，覃墟相距十餘裡，為犄角。

translations.literal: Dingfeng's old nest was called Pingtian Stockade, relying on mountain peril with layered palisades, defended by great cannon; Tanxu was separated by more than ten li, forming a horn pincer.
translations.idiomatic: Dingfeng's stronghold was Pingtian Stockade, fortified on mountainous terrain with multiple palisades and heavy guns; Tanxu, more than ten li away, formed a supporting redoubt.

sentences.zh: 坤一陽議撫，撤軍回貴縣，潛師夜襲覃墟，遂圍平天寨，复橫州，鼎鳳勢蹙。

translations.literal: Kunyi openly discussed pacification, withdrew troops back to Guixian, secretly sent troops in night assault on Tanxu, then besieged Pingtian Stockade, recovered Hengzhou, and Dingfeng's situation grew cramped.
translations.idiomatic: Kunyi feigned interest in negotiation, withdrew to Guixian, then launched a night raid on Tanxu, besieged Pingtian Stockade, retook Hengzhou, and cornered Dingfeng.

sentences.zh: 三年四月，擒鼎鳳及其黨誅之。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the third year, Dingfeng and his party were captured and executed.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the third year he captured Dingfeng and his followers and executed them.

sentences.zh: 潯州平，賜號碩勇巴圖魯。

translations.literal: Xunzhou was pacified and he was granted the title Sure Valiant Baturu.
translations.idiomatic: With Xunzhou pacified, he was granted the title Sure Valiant Baturu.

sentences.zh: 四年，剿平思恩、南寧土匪，复永淳，擢江西巡撫。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, he suppressed and pacified bandits in Si'en and Nanning, recovered Yongchun, and was promoted to Jiangxi governor.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he stamped out bandits in Si'en and Nanning, recovered Yongchun, and was made Jiangxi governor.

sentences.zh: 令席寶田、黃少春會剿粵匪餘黨於閩邊，五年，聚殲於廣東嘉應州，加頭品頂戴。

translations.literal: He ordered Xi Baotian and Huang Shaochun to join in suppressing remaining Guangdong rebels at the Fujian border; in the fifth year they were gathered and annihilated at Jiayingzhou in Guangdong; he received the first-class official's cap button.
translations.idiomatic: He had Xi Baotian and Huang Shaochun cooperate in clearing Guangdong rebel remnants on the Fujian border; in the fifth year they destroyed them at Jiaying in Guangdong, and Kunyi received the first-rank official cap.

sentences.zh: 軍事既定，坤一治尚安靜，因整頓丁漕，不便於紳戶。

translations.literal: After military affairs were settled, Kunyi's governance favored quiet; because he rectified corvée and grain transport duties, it was inconvenient for gentry households.
translations.idiomatic: Once the fighting ended, Kunyi governed lightly but tightened the land tax and grain transport levies, which displeased the local gentry.

sentences.zh: 十一年，左都御史胡家玉疏劾之，坤一奏家玉積欠漕糧，又屢貽書干預地方事。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, left censor-in-chief Hu Jiayu memorialized impeaching him; Kunyi memorialized that Jiayu had long owed transport grain taxes and repeatedly sent letters interfering in local affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year the left censor-in-chief Hu Jiayu impeached him; Kunyi responded that Hu owed years of transport grain payments and had repeatedly meddled in local administration by letter.

sentences.zh: 詔兩斥之，家玉獲譴，坤一亦坐先不上聞，部議降三級調用，加恩改革職留任，降三品頂戴。

translations.literal: An edict rebuked both; Jiayu was punished, Kunyi also sat for not reporting first; the ministry deliberated demotion three ranks and transfer, but grace reformed it to retention in office with demoted third-rank cap button.
translations.idiomatic: The throne rebuked them both; Hu was punished, but Kunyi was faulted for not reporting earlier—the ministry proposed demoting him three ranks, though by grace he kept his post with a third-rank cap.

sentences.zh: 尋復之，命署兩江總督。

translations.literal: Soon it was restored, and he was ordered to act as Liangjiang governor-general.
translations.idiomatic: His rank was soon restored, and he was appointed acting Liangjiang governor-general.

sentences.zh: 光緒元年，擢兩廣總督。

translations.literal: In the first year of Guangxu, he was promoted to Liangguang governor-general.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Guangxu he was promoted to Liangguang governor-general.

sentences.zh: 廣東號為富穰，庫儲實空，出入不能相抵。

translations.literal: Guangdong was known as rich and fertile, but treasury stores were in fact empty and income and expenditure could not balance.
translations.idiomatic: Guangdong had a reputation for wealth, but the treasury was empty and income could not cover outlays.

sentences.zh: 議者請加鹽釐及洋藥稅，坤一以加鹽釐則官引愈滯，但嚴緝私販，以暢銷路；

translations.literal: Discussants requested increased salt levy and foreign medicine tax; Kunyi considered that increasing salt levy would make official salt convoys more stagnant, but only strictly suppress private trafficking to open sales routes;
translations.idiomatic: Some proposed raising the salt surcharge and opium duty; Kunyi argued that raising the salt levy would only slow official sales further, and that strict interdiction of smuggling would suffice to restore the market;

sentences.zh: 又援成案，籌款收買餘鹽，發商交運，官民交便。

translations.literal: moreover citing precedent cases, raised funds to purchase surplus salt and release to merchants for transport, officials and people both convenient.
translations.idiomatic: citing precedents, he raised funds to buy up surplus salt and release it to merchants for transport, benefiting both government and traders.

sentences.zh: 藥釐抽收，各地輕重不同，改歸一律，無加稅之名，歲增鉅萬。

translations.literal: Medicine levy collection differed in weight across places; changed to uniform regulation without the name of added tax, yearly increase of millions.
translations.idiomatic: Opium duties varied by region; he standardized them nationwide without formally raising the rate, yet added millions to annual revenue.

sentences.zh: 吏治重在久任，令實缺各歸本任，不輕更調。

translations.literal: Official governance emphasizes long tenure; he ordered that substantive vacancies each return to their original posts, not lightly transferred.
translations.idiomatic: Good administration depends on continuity in office; he kept substantive appointees in their posts and avoided frequent rotations.

sentences.zh: 禁賭以絕盜源，水陸緝捕各營，分定地段以專責成，盜發輒獲。

translations.literal: Prohibiting gambling to cut off the source of bandits, water and land arrest camps each assigned fixed districts for exclusive responsibility, bandits arising were promptly captured.
translations.idiomatic: He banned gambling to dry up crime at its source, assigned land and water patrol units to fixed districts with clear accountability, and bandits were usually caught when they struck.

sentences.zh: 二年，調授兩江總督。

translations.literal: In the second year, transferred and appointed Liangjiang governor-general.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was transferred to Liangjiang governor-general.

sentences.zh: 六年，俄羅斯以交還伊犁，藉端要挾。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, Russia used the return of Ili as a pretext for coercion.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year Russia used the return of Ili as leverage for extortion.

sentences.zh: 詔籌防務，坤一上疏，略謂：「東三省無久經戰陣之宿將勁旅，急宜綢繆。

translations.literal: An edict ordered defense preparations; Kunyi submitted a memorial stating in summary: "The three eastern provinces lack veteran generals and crack troops long seasoned in battle; urgent measures must be laid in advance.
translations.idiomatic: Ordered to prepare defenses, Kunyi memorialized that the Three Eastern Provinces lacked battle-tested commanders and troops and needed urgent reinforcement.

sentences.zh: 西北既戒嚴，東南不可復生波折。

translations.literal: The northwest is already on alert; the southeast must not again produce disturbances.
translations.idiomatic: With the northwest already on alert, the southeast cannot afford new troubles.

sentences.zh: 日本、琉球之事宜早結束，勿使與俄人合以謀我。

translations.literal: Affairs of Japan and Ryukyu should be concluded early, lest they join with Russians to plot against us.
translations.idiomatic: Disputes with Japan over Ryukyu should be settled quickly, lest Japan align with Russia against us.

sentences.zh: 英、德諸國與俄猜忌日深，應如何結為聲援，以伺俄人之後。

translations.literal: England, Germany, and other states grow daily deeper in suspicion of Russia; how they should be joined as vocal support to watch Russia's rear should be considered.
translations.idiomatic: Britain and Germany are increasingly at odds with Russia—how can we enlist them as counterweights and threaten Russia's rear?

sentences.zh: 凡此皆賴廟謨廣運，神而明之。」

translations.literal: All these depend on the court's broad deliberation, discerning with spirit."
translations.idiomatic: All of this depends on far-sighted deliberation in the inner court.

sentences.zh: 九年，法越構釁，邊事戒嚴。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, France and Vietnam provoked conflict; frontier affairs were placed on alert.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year France and Vietnam clashed, and the frontier was placed on alert.

sentences.zh: 坤一疏：「請由廣東、廣西遴派明幹大員統勁旅出關，駐紮諒山等處，以助剿土匪為名，密與越南共籌防禦。

translations.literal: Kunyi memorialized: "Request selection from Guangdong and Guangxi of capable major officials to command crack troops out of the passes, garrisoned at Lang Son and other places, under the name of assisting in suppressing local bandits, secretly jointly with Vietnam to plan defense.
translations.idiomatic: Kunyi proposed: "Select able officials from Guangdong and Guangxi to lead strong forces across the border to garrison Lang Son and similar points, ostensibly to help suppress bandits but in fact to coordinate defenses secretly with Vietnam.

sentences.zh: 並令越南招太原、宣光黑旗賊眾，免為法人誘用。

translations.literal: And order Vietnam to recruit Taiyuan and Xuangang Black Flag bandit masses, lest they be enticed for use by the French.
translations.idiomatic: Have Vietnam recruit the Black Flag bands of Taiyuan and Xuangang so the French cannot enlist them.

sentences.zh: 雲南據險設​​奇，以資犄角。

translations.literal: Yunnan should hold strategic passes and deploy extraordinary tactics to serve as pincer horns.
translations.idiomatic: Yunnan should hold the mountain passes and keep irregular forces in reserve as a flank.

sentences.zh: 法人知我有備，其謀自沮。

translations.literal: When the French know we have preparations, their plots will naturally abate.
translations.idiomatic: Once the French see we are prepared, their designs will stall of themselves.

sentences.zh: 雲南方擬加重越南貨稅，決不可行。

translations.literal: Yunnan's side proposed increasing Vietnam goods taxes; this absolutely cannot be carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Yunnan's plan to raise duties on Vietnamese goods is absolutely unacceptable.

sentences.zh: 重稅能施之越人，不能施之法人。

translations.literal: Heavy taxes can be applied to Vietnamese but cannot be applied to the French.
translations.idiomatic: Heavier taxes might be levied on Vietnamese merchants, but not on the French.

sentences.zh: 越人倘因此轉嗾法人入滇通商，得以依託假冒，如沿海奸商故智，不可不慮。

translations.literal: If Vietnamese therefore turn to egg on the French to enter Yunnan for trade, relying on impersonation and fraud, like coastal crafty merchants' old tricks, this cannot go unconsidered.
translations.idiomatic: Vietnamese might then induce the French to enter Yunnan under treaty cover by proxy, repeating the ruses of coastal smugglers—this must be guarded against.

sentences.zh: 越南如果與法別立新約，中國縱不能禁，亦應使其慎重；

translations.literal: If Vietnam separately concludes a new treaty with France, China though unable to forbid it, should still make them cautious;
translations.idiomatic: If Vietnam negotiates a separate treaty with France, China may be unable to forbid it but should urge caution;

sentences.zh: 或即指示機宜，免致再誤。

translations.literal: or immediately instruct the opportune course, lest again err.
translations.idiomatic: or offer timely guidance so they do not blunder again.

sentences.zh: 越南​​積弱，若不早為扶持，覆亡立待。

translations.literal: Vietnam long accumulated weakness; if not early supported, collapse awaits immediately.
translations.idiomatic: Vietnam has been weak for generations; without early support, its fall is imminent.

sentences.zh: 滇、粵籓籬盡失，逼處堪虞。

translations.literal: Yunnan and Guangdong screen barriers entirely lost, pressed close and worthy of worry.
translations.idiomatic: Once Yunnan and Guangdong lose their buffer, the threat presses directly on our border.

sentences.zh: 與其補救於後，曷若慎防於先。

translations.literal: Rather than remedying afterward, how much better to guard cautiously beforehand.
translations.idiomatic: Better to guard against disaster beforehand than to pick up the pieces afterward.

sentences.zh: 此不可不明目張膽以提挈者也。」

translations.literal: This cannot but be openly and boldly raised up and led."
translations.idiomatic: China must take the lead openly, not shrink from guiding Vietnam.

sentences.zh: 疏入，多被採納。

translations.literal: When the memorial entered, much was adopted.
translations.idiomatic: Much of the memorial was adopted when it reached the throne.

sentences.zh: 十二年，丁繼母憂。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, he entered mourning for his stepmother.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he mourned his stepmother.

sentences.zh: 十六年，仍授兩江總督。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, still appointed Liangjiang governor-general.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he was again appointed Liangjiang governor-general.

sentences.zh: 十七年，命幫辦海軍事務。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, ordered to assist in naval affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he was ordered to assist in naval affairs.

sentences.zh: 二十年，皇太后萬壽，賜雙眼花翎。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year, on the Empress Dowager's ten-thousand-year birthday, granted double-eyed peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year, for the Empress Dowager's birthday celebration, he was awarded the double-eyed peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 日本犯遼東，九連城、鳳凰城、金州、旅順悉陷，北洋海陸軍皆失利。

translations.literal: Japan invaded eastern Liaodong; Jiuliancheng, Fengcheng, Jinzhou, and Lüshun all fell; Northern Seas land and naval armies all suffered defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Japan invaded eastern Liaodong; Jiuliancheng, Fengcheng, Jinzhou, and Port Arthur all fell, and the Beiyang land and naval forces were defeated throughout.

sentences.zh: 召坤一至京，命為欽差大臣，督關內外防剿諸軍。

translations.literal: Kunyi was summoned to the capital and appointed imperial commissioner to supervise all armies defending and suppressing within and beyond the passes.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kunyi was called to Beijing and made imperial commissioner to direct all forces guarding and fighting along the northeastern frontier.

sentences.zh: 坤一謂兵未集，械未備，不能輕試，詔促之出關。

translations.literal: Kunyi said the troops were not yet gathered and weapons not yet prepared and one could not lightly try battle; an edict urged him to go out beyond the pass.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kunyi argued that troops and arms were not ready and that a premature offensive would be reckless; the court ordered him to march out all the same.

sentences.zh: 時已遣使議和，坤一以兩宮意見未洽為憂，瀕行，語師傅翁同龢曰：「公調和之責，比餘軍事為重也。」

translations.literal: Envoys had already been sent to negotiate peace; Kunyi worried that the views of the two palaces were not in harmony; on the eve of departure he said to tutor Weng Tonghe: "Your duty of mediation is weightier than all other military affairs."
translations.idiomatic: Peace envoys were already abroad, and Liu Kunyi feared discord between the empress dowagers. Before leaving he told Weng Tonghe, the emperor's tutor: "Your task of reconciling the court matters more than anything I can do in the field."

sentences.zh: 二十一年春，前敵宋慶、吳大澂等复屢敗，新募諸軍實不能任戰，日本議和要挾彌甚，下坤一與直隸總督王文韶決和戰之策。

translations.literal: In the spring of the twenty-first year the forward commanders Song Qing, Wu Dacheng, and others again suffered repeated defeats; the newly recruited armies truly could not bear battle; Japan's peace demands grew ever harsher; Kunyi and Zhili governor-general Wang Wenshao were ordered to decide the policy of peace or war.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the twenty-first year Song Qing, Wu Dacheng, and other front commanders were beaten again and again; the new levies proved useless in battle; Japan's peace terms grew harsher by the day. Liu Kunyi and Zhili governor Wang Wenshao were ordered to settle whether to fight on or sue for peace.

sentences.zh: 坤一以身任軍事，仍主戰而不堅執。

translations.literal: Kunyi personally bore military responsibility and still favored war but did not insist rigidly.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kunyi took military responsibility on himself and still leaned toward continuing the war, but did not cling to that view obstinately.

sentences.zh: 未幾和議成，回任。

translations.literal: Before long peace was concluded and he returned to his post.
translations.idiomatic: Peace was soon signed, and he returned to his governorship.

sentences.zh: 坤一素多病，臥治江南，事持大體。

translations.literal: Kunyi had long been ill and governed Jiangnan from his bed, handling affairs by grasping the large principles.
translations.idiomatic: Chronically ill, Liu Kunyi often governed Jiangnan from his sickbed, keeping his eye on essentials rather than detail.

sentences.zh: 言者論其左右用事，詔誡其不可偏信，振刷精神，以任艱鉅。

translations.literal: Critics spoke of his close associates wielding power; an edict admonished him not to trust them partially, to rouse his spirit, and to bear grave responsibilities.
translations.idiomatic: Critics said his favorites were running affairs; the throne warned him not to trust them blindly, to shake off his lassitude, and to meet the heavy duties before him.

sentences.zh: 坤一屢疏陳情乞退，不許。

translations.literal: Kunyi repeatedly memorialized stating his feelings and begging to retire; permission was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized again and again asking to retire; each time the court refused.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，立溥俊為穆宗嗣子，朝野洶洶，謂將有廢立事，坤一致書大學士榮祿曰：「君臣之分久定，中外之口宜防。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year Pujun was established as heir son to Emperor Muzong; court and country were in uproar, saying there would be an affair of deposition and installation; Kunyi wrote to grand secretary Ronglu: "The distinction between ruler and minister has long been fixed; mouths at home and abroad should be guarded against.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year Pujun was named heir to Emperor Muzong, and rumor swept the empire that the throne itself might be at stake. Liu Kunyi wrote to Grand Secretary Ronglu: "The bond between sovereign and subject is settled; we must not give scandal a foothold at home or abroad.

sentences.zh: 坤一所以報國在此，所以報公亦在此。」

translations.literal: Kunyi's way of repaying the state lies here, and his way of repaying you lies here as well."
translations.idiomatic: That is how I serve the dynasty—and how I repay your trust."

sentences.zh: 二十六年，值德宗萬壽，加太子太保。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year, on the occasion of Emperor Dezong's birthday celebration, he was made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year, on the emperor's birthday, he was promoted to Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 拳匪亂起，坤一偕李鴻章、張之洞創議，會東南疆吏與各國領事訂約，互為保護，人心始定。

translations.literal: When the Boxer turmoil arose, Kunyi together with Li Hongzhang and Zhang Zhidong initiated a proposal; southeastern governors met with foreign consuls to conclude treaties of mutual protection, and popular feeling at last settled.
translations.idiomatic: When the Boxer rising broke out, Liu Kunyi joined Li Hongzhang and Zhang Zhidong in a plan for the southeast: local officials and foreign consuls agreed to protect one another's jurisdictions, and public panic subsided.

sentences.zh: 車駕西幸，議者或請遷都西安，坤一復偕各督撫力陳其不可，籥請回鑾。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage went west on tour, some advisers urged moving the capital to Xi'an; Kunyi again joined the various governors in strongly stating this was impossible and earnestly begged the court to return.
translations.idiomatic: When the court fled west, some urged moving the capital to Xi'an; Liu Kunyi and the other governors protested vigorously and pleaded for the emperor's return to Beijing.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，偕張之洞會議請變法，以興學為首務，中法之應整頓變通者十二事，西法之應兼採並用者十一事，聯銜分三疏上之。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year he joined Zhang Zhidong in conference to request reform, taking promotion of learning as the first task; twelve matters in which Chinese methods should be rectified and changed, and eleven Western methods that should be adopted and used together, were submitted in three joint memorials.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year he and Zhang Zhidong jointly proposed reform, putting education first: twelve items for reviving Chinese institutions and eleven for adopting Western practices, set out in three co-signed memorials.

sentences.zh: 詔下政務處議行，是為實行變法之始。

translations.literal: An edict sent the proposals to the Bureau of Government Affairs for deliberation and implementation; this was the beginning of putting reform into practice.
translations.idiomatic: The court referred the proposals to the Bureau of Government Affairs, marking the start of the reform program.

sentences.zh: 洎回鑾，施恩疆吏，加太子太保。

translations.literal: When the court returned, grace was extended to frontier officials and he was again made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: After the emperor's return, frontier officials were rewarded, and Liu Kunyi was again made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，卒，優詔賜卹。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year he died and a gracious edict granted mourning benefits.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year he died, and the court granted generous funeral honors.

sentences.zh: 嘉其秉性公忠，才猷宏遠，保障東南，厥功尤著，追封一等男爵，贈太傅，賜金治喪，命江寧將軍致祭，特諡忠誠。

translations.literal: He was praised for his upright loyal nature, far-reaching talent and planning, and especially for securing the southeast; he was posthumously enfeoffed as a first-rank baron, made Grand Tutor, granted gold for the funeral, the Jiangning general was ordered to offer sacrifice, and was specially given the posthumous title Zhongcheng.
translations.idiomatic: The court praised his integrity, breadth of vision, and above all his defense of the southeast; he was posthumously created a first-class baron, made Grand Tutor, given funds for his funeral, honored with sacrifices by the Jiangning general, and named Zhongcheng posthumously.

sentences.zh: 祀賢良祠，原籍、立功省建專祠。

translations.literal: He was enshrined in the Hall of Worthy Officials, and special shrines were built in his native place and the provinces where he had won merit.
translations.idiomatic: He was enshrined in the Hall of Worthy Officials, with commemorative temples in his home province and every province where he had served.

sentences.zh: 賜其子能紀四品京堂，諸孫並予官。

translations.literal: His son Nengji was granted a fourth-rank post in the capital bureaucracy, and all grandsons were also given offices.
translations.idiomatic: His son Nengji received a fourth-rank capital post, and his grandsons were given official rank as well.

sentences.zh: 張之洞疏陳坤一居官廉靜寬厚，不求赫赫之名，而身際艱危，維持大局，毅然擔當，從不推諉，其忠定明決，能斷大事，有古名臣風。

translations.literal: Zhang Zhidong memorialized that Kunyi in office was incorrupt, calm, and generous, did not seek resounding fame, yet when personally facing peril maintained the overall situation, resolutely bore responsibility and never shirked; his loyalty was steadfast and his decisions clear, able to decide great affairs, with the air of ancient renowned ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhidong wrote that Liu Kunyi governed with quiet integrity and generosity, sought no fame, yet in crisis held the realm together, shouldered responsibility without excuse, and decided great matters with the steadiness of the statesmen of old.

sentences.zh: 世以所言為允。

translations.literal: The age held his words to be just.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries agreed that this was fair.

sentences.zh: 論曰：曾國荃當蘇、浙未復，孤軍直搗金陵，在兵事為危機，其成功由於堅忍。

translations.literal: The commentary says: When Zeng Guoquan, while Jiangsu and Zhejiang were not yet recovered, led a lone army straight against Jinling, in military affairs it was a crisis, and his success came from steadfast endurance.
translations.idiomatic: The historians comment: When Jiangsu and Zhejiang were still in rebel hands, Zeng Guoquan drove a single column straight at Nanjing—the riskiest move in the war—and won through sheer tenacity.

sentences.zh: 鏟其本根，則枝蔓自絕，信不世之勳也。

translations.literal: Uproot the root and the branches wither of themselves—truly a merit not of a single age.
translations.idiomatic: Cut out the root and the branches die on their own—a feat unmatched in his generation.

sentences.zh: 屢退復起，朝廷倚為保障，以功名終。

translations.literal: Repeatedly retiring and returning to service, the court relied on him as a bulwark, and he ended in fame and rank.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned and returned to duty more than once; the court leaned on him as a pillar of the realm, and he finished his career in honor.

sentences.zh: 沈葆楨清望冠時，力任艱鉅，兵略、吏治並卓然。

translations.literal: Shen Baozhen's pure reputation stood first in his time; he vigorously bore grave responsibilities, and both military strategy and civil administration were outstanding.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Baozhen's moral authority stood above his peers; he took on the hardest tasks, excelling equally in war and in civil government.

sentences.zh: 其手創船政，精果一時無耦。

translations.literal: The naval administration he founded with his own hand was so precise and effective that for a time none could match it.
translations.idiomatic: The navy yard he built from nothing was run with an efficiency none could rival at the time.

sentences.zh: 後來不能充拓，且聽廢棄，豈非因任事之難其人哉？

translations.literal: Later it could not be expanded and was even allowed to fall into disuse—is this not because it is hard to find the right man for such a task?
translations.idiomatic: Later it was neither expanded nor properly maintained—is that not because such work demands a leader of rare caliber?

sentences.zh: 劉坤一起家軍旅，謀國獨見其大，晚年勳望，幾軼同儕，房、杜謀斷之功，不與褒、鄂並論矣。

translations.literal: Liu Kunyi rose from the military life; in planning for the state he alone saw the large view; in his later years his merit and standing nearly surpassed his peers; the merit of Fang and Du in counsel and decision cannot be discussed together with Bao and E.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kunyi rose through the army yet always thought in terms of the whole empire; in his last years his stature nearly eclipsed his contemporaries. As strategists he belongs with Fang Xuanling and Du Ruhui rather than with mere battlefield champions like Bao Xin and E Yi.
